Ces avantages sont peut-tre encore plus prcieux pour les pays voisins, puisque 50 d'entre eux (dont ceux de la zone franc) ont dj adopt l'euro comme monnaie de 5 Ex : Russie, Ukraine, Core, Japon, Chine, pays de lOPEP. 6 Ex : Russie, Ukraine, Core, Japon, Chine, pays de lOPEP. 18 rfrence pour leurs rgimes de change, soit comme ancre unique (dans 30 cas environ), soit comme composante d'un panier de monnaies.  L'utilisation de l'euro dans les rgimes de change des pays tiers concerne essentiellement des rgions qui ont tiss des liens troits avec la zone euro ou qui ont mis en place des arrangements institutionnels spciaux avec l'UE (pays adhrents et candidats, Balkans, Afrique du nord et zone franc). Dans tous les cas, ces rgimes de change rsultent d'une dcision unilatrale, qui n'implique aucun engagement de la part de l'Eurosystme. Cependant, des liens troits avec l'euro peuvent prsenter lavantage, pour ces pays, d' importer  de la crdibilit,  condition de poursuivre simultanment des politiques appropries.  En ce qui concerne les dix nouveaux pays de l'UE, laissez-moi souligner que le critre de stabilit des taux de change au sein du MCE II ncessite que cette stabilit soit atteinte avant l'adoption de la monnaie unique. L'avantage est que l'adoption de l'euro sera le couronnement d'un processus de convergence structur au sein d'un cadre multilatral. C'est assurment l'un des dfis les plus importants auxquels devra faire face la zone euro dans les annes  venir. B.3. La position de lEurosystme sur le dveloppement du rle international de leuro  LEurosystme observe une position officielle de neutralit vis--vis du dveloppement externe de sa monnaie, ce qui signifie quil ne promeut ni nempche le dveloppement du rle international de leuro, car il considre que cest un processus essentiellement conduit par les marchs.  En outre, lEurosystme est conscient de la ncessit dviter des volutions trop brutales, qui pourraient entraner une volatilit excessive ou des msalignements des taux de change.  En fait, la conduite dune politique montaire oriente vers le maintien de la stabilit des prix est la meilleure contribution que lEurosystme puisse apporter au dveloppement 19 international de sa monnaie, car elle favorise la confiance dans la valeur de leuro et renforce la crdibilit de la zone. PARTIE 3 : LES DFIS DE LA MONNAIE UNIQUE L'environnement dans lequel volue l'euro tant en mutation continue, les pouvoirs publics doivent faire face  de nouveaux dfis lorsqu'ils formulent et mettent en uvre leurs dcisions de politique conomique. Je voudrais attirer l'attention sur trois de ces dfis qui,  mon avis, pseront fortement sur l'avenir de l'euro et de la construction europenne. En premier lieu, il est ncessaire de renforcer la coordination budgtaire de l'UE afin de consolider les fondements sur lesquels repose l'euro (A), dans une priode o les politiques budgtaires en Europe doivent faire face  des dfis spcifiques tels que le vieillissement de la population. En deuxime lieu, il est ncessaire de mettre en uvre des rformes structurelles (B) afin de mieux prparer les pays  affronter les dfis  venir. Enfin, le processus d'largissement (C), qui est certes dj une ralit, demandera des efforts supplmentaires pour que les nouveaux tats membres progressent encore et finissent par rattraper leur retard. A. La ncessit d'un renforcement de la cohsion et de la coordination budgtaires au sein de l'Union  Le respect des rgles et des procdures formules dans le Trait et des dispositions du Pacte de stabilit et de croissance imposent la mme discipline budgtaire  tous les tats membres : le dficit budgtaire ne doit pas excder le plafond de 3 % du PIB et le ratio d'endettement total ne devrait pas dpasser 60 % du PIB. Ces limites contribuent  assurer un policy-mix optimal au niveau de la zone euro, dans la mesure o une politique budgtaire laxiste risque,  terme, de compromettre la ralisation de la stabilit des prix. Enfin, elles entretiennent une croissance et un emploi durables et sont propices  la stabilit conomique. 20  La discipline budgtaire est en effet d'une importance capitale pour l'UEM, car elle est un corollaire ncessaire de la politique montaire unique. On attend des tats membres qu'ils considrent leurs politiques conomiques comme des questions  d'intrt commun , tant donn l'incidence que leurs dcisions budgtaires peuvent avoir sur la zone euro dans son ensemble. Dans une union montaire, il est de la plus grande importance dviter les  comportements de passager clandestin , d'o la clause de  non-renflouement  inscrite dans le Trait de Maastricht.  Le cadre institutionnel de la coordination des politiques conomiques nationales a bien fonctionn dans le pass, en laissant une marge de manuvre suffisante pour faire face  un ralentissement de la croissance. Conformment au concept d'quilibre des soldes budgtaires structurels, les tats membres de l'UE se sont engags  atteindre et  maintenir, au cours du cycle conomique, une situation budgtaire  proche de l'quilibre ou excdentaire . Cette exigence doit permettre de faire face aux chocs asymtriques et aux fluctuations conjoncturelles, tout en laissant les stabilisateurs automatiques exercer pleinement leurs effets. Cette flexibilit est essentielle pour surmonter les chocs asymtriques tout en prservant la soutenabilit  long terme des finances publiques et l'autonomie de la politique montaire.  Cependant, les difficults auxquelles se sont heurts de nombreux pays europens ont suscit de vives critiques  lencontre des dispositions budgtaires du Trait et du Pacte de stabilit et de croissance. Dans ce contexte, la Commission europenne a prsent en septembre dernier des propositions de rforme ; les discussions en Conseil des Ministres ont finalement abouti en mars et laccord sur cette rforme, qui vise  modifier les modalits de la mise en uvre du Pacte, a t entrin lors du Conseil europen des 22-23 mars dernier. Ces modifications portent principalement sur deux aspects : le volet prventif et le volet correctif du Pacte :  Sur le volet prventif, la modification la plus intressante a consist  rechercher une application plus symtrique du Pacte, en priode de basse et de haute conjoncture, en incitant les Etats membres  renforcer la mise en uvre d'une politique budgtaire saine en priode de haute conjoncture. Lorsque la croissance est forte, les pays doivent se mobiliser encore davantage pour rduire leurs dficits ou dgager des excdents et rduire ainsi l'encours d'une dette publique, souvent  des niveaux levs. Cela signifie 21 qu'en priode de conjoncture favorable, il faut adopter des politiques budgtaires moins laxistes pour garantir la soutenabilit  long terme des finances publiques. En revanche dautres modifications, comme la diffrenciation par pays de lobjectif de moyen terme, ou la prise en compte de limpact de rformes structurelles -par exemple des rgimes de retraites- sont discutables, notamment parce quelles sont susceptibles daccrotre la complexit du Pacte et dattnuer lefficacit du volet prventif.  Sur le volet correctif (cest--dire concernant la mise en uvre de la procdure pour dficit excessif  lgard dun Etat membre ne respectant pas les valeurs de rfrence de 3% et 60%), les modifications introduites aboutissent clairement  un assouplissement du Pacte. On peut citer par exemple, la nouvelle dfinition des  circonstances exceptionnelles et temporaires , qui permet dviter le dclenchement de la procdure pour dficit excessif ds lors que le taux de croissance est ngatif ou trs faible par rapport au potentiel. Il faut galement noter la dfinition dune liste de  facteurs pertinents  -dont il est tenu compte pour apprcier le dpassement du dficit public audel de la valeur de rfrence de 3 % du PIB- qui comporte notamment les dpenses de recherche et dveloppement, laide public au dveloppement ainsi que les dpenses lies  la rforme des systmes de retraite ou lunification de lEurope. Enfin, il faut souligner un allongement gnral des dlais accords aux Etats pour la correction du dficit excessif.  A la suite de cet accord du Conseil des Ministres sur lamlioration de la mise en uvre du Pacte, le Conseil des Gouverneurs de la BCE sest exprim publiquement pour exprimer ses proccupations. Il a rappel que des politiques budgtaires saines et une politique montaire axe sur la stabilit des prix sont essentielles pour le succs de lUnion conomique et montaire. Elles constituent des conditions indispensables  la stabilit macroconomique,  la croissance et  la cohsion dans la zone euro. Le Conseil des Gouverneurs de la BCE a insist sur le fait quil est impratif que les tats membres, la Commission europenne et le Conseil de lUnion europenne mettent en uvre le cadre rvis dune manire rigoureuse et cohrente, propice  la conduite de politiques budgtaires prudentes. Le respect de l'objectif central d'quilibre budgtaire reste d'autant plus indispensable que l'Union europenne devra s'atteler au problme du vieillissement 22 rapide de la population, dont les implications sur les finances publiques sont considrables, tant sous l'angle des dpenses de sant que des rgimes de retraite. tant donn que, dans ces domaines, les rformes risquent de n'tre perceptibles qu' moyen et long termes, il est essentiel que les pays europens prennent toutes les dispositions ncessaires pour prvenir les consquences de ces volutions dmographiques, notamment sur le plan budgtaire.  La mise en uvre de politiques budgtaires saines passe galement par l'amlioration de la qualit des dpenses publiques. Un premier pas dans cette direction consisterait  faire porter le processus d'ajustement sur les dpenses courantes plutt que sur l'investissement,  la diffrence de ce qui a t fait dans la plupart des pays  la fin des annes quatre-vingt-dix. De manire plus gnrale, les pays de lUE doivent entreprendre des rformes structurelles visant  renforcer le potentiel de croissance et  favoriser la cration d'emplois. Sur ces points, l'Eurosystme a appel ces pays  maintes reprises et sans ambigut possible  procder  ces rformes. B. Des rformes structurelles doivent tre accomplies dans plusieurs domaines Il subsiste nanmoins en Europe, en particulier dans la zone euro, d'importantes rigidits structurelles qu'il s'agit de rsoudre si l'on souhaite promouvoir la plus forte croissance non inflationniste possible. Je souhaiterais ici voquer plusieurs pistes qui font d'ailleurs l'objet d'un consensus au sein du Conseil des gouverneurs de la zone euro. Elles portent notamment sur les efforts  poursuivre en ce qui concerne le rle et l'importance de la recherche (B1) pour accrotre le potentiel de croissance de la zone euro, le dveloppement des  forces d'agglomration  pour faciliter la localisation des entreprises (B2), les efforts  accomplir enfin pour accrotre la flexibilit sur le march du travail (B3) et l'intgration des marchs des biens et services (B4). B.1. Une conomie fonde sur la connaissance S'agissant du premier point, la stratgie adopte  l'unanimit lors du Conseil europen de Lisbonne en mars 2000, qui a pour objectif de faire de l'Union europenne  l'conomie de la connaissance la plus comptitive et la plus dynamique du monde, capable d'une croissance conomique durable accompagne d'une amlioration qualitative et quantitative de l'emploi 23 et d'une plus grande cohsion sociale , fournit un cadre de rfrence pour guider l'action publique. Elle insiste notamment sur l'importance de la recherche, de l'innovation et de la diffusion des technologies nouvelles pour lever le niveau de productivit de l'conomie. Elle vise galement  donner  l'conomie europenne ainsi qu' tous les pays membres de l'UE plus de souplesse, plus d'activit, et plus d'emplois. Il s'agit d'une stratgie certes ambitieuse mais cruciale pour l'avenir de l'Europe et de la zone euro. B.2. La comptitivit des entreprises Dans ce contexte, en raison notamment de la concurrence internationale, il est galement crucial de dvelopper les  forces d'agglomration , c'est--dire les incitations qui forcent les entreprises  se concentrer gographiquement pour bnficier d'conomies d'chelle et externes. L'existence d'une zone  pouvoir d'achat lev est notamment l'un des facteurs importants de la localisation des entreprises europennes. J'ai dj mentionn les forces d'attractivit de la zone euro mais il nous faut aller plus loin encore, en particulier en ce qui concerne la matrise des cots, notamment salariaux, et la ncessit d'assurer un environnement favorable  la comptitivit des entreprises europennes. En effet, les emplois sont crs de prfrence dans les conomies qui savent modrer leurs cots unitaires de production et offrir un environnement aussi favorable que possible  la comptitivit des entreprises. Cela suppose donc que soient poursuivies, les rformes structurelles sur le march du travail et celui des biens et des services. B.3. La flexibilit sur le march du travail  En ce qui concerne le march du travail, la zone euro est caractrise par un faible taux d'emploi, suprieur  63 % en 2004 contre 75 % aux tats-Unis, ce qui se traduit par une perte non ngligeable en termes de PIB par habitant (prs de 25 % infrieur  celui des tats-Unis). Ce bas taux d'emploi rsulte du niveau lev du chmage dans la zone euro, proche de 9 % actuellement et surtout de la faiblesse du taux d'activit.  Le chmage en Europe tant pour l'essentiel d'origine structurelle, il importe ds lors de fluidifier le march du travail et de prserver une structure d'incitations permettant d'lever le taux d'activit. Cela suppose notamment que soient mises en 24 uvre des mesures visant  rduire le cot du travail, les charges des entreprises mais galement que soient promues des structures d'incitations  destination des actifs parmi les classes d'ges les plus jeunes mais galement les plus ges ainsi que pour les moins qualifis. Contrairement  ce que l'on observe aux tats-Unis, o existe une longue tradition de mobilit professionnelle et gographique, les diffrences culturelles et linguistiques constituent encore un frein  la mobilit du facteur travail en Europe. La faiblesse de la mobilit professionnelle et gographique dpend galement d'une diffrentiation sans doute insuffisante des salaires dans les pays de la zone euro qui permettraient de mieux reflter les diffrences en termes de gains de productivit ou de dveloppement entre rgions ou secteurs d'activit. B.4. L'intgration des marchs des biens et services  L'accroissement du niveau de productivit dans la zone euro repose galement sur l'approfondissement des rformes sur le march des biens et services car le retard europen, vis--vis notamment des tats-Unis, trouve galement son origine dans la prsence de rigidits structurelles lies  l'existence de barrires  l'entre sur ce march. Or, en l'absence de pressions concurrentielles, les entreprises ne sont gure incites  accrotre leur efficacit.  Des rformes rglementaires doivent donc tre entreprises tant au niveau des pays membres qu'au niveau de l'Union conomique dans son ensemble. D'aprs les travaux de recherche conduits sous l'gide du CEPR et de l'Eurosystme, la cration du march unique a dj constitu une tape majeure mais l'objectif reste bien celui d'une intgration complte du march des biens et services au niveau europen. Cela concerne notamment le secteur des services o, il faut bien le reconnatre, les progrs ont t moins nets que dans les autres secteurs d'activit. Certes, cela s'explique encore pour partie par des diffrences culturelles. Il reste que les pouvoirs publics, au niveau national comme au niveau communautaire, doivent poursuivre leurs efforts et favoriser le degr de concurrence et d'intgration dans tous les secteurs d'activit. Je mentionnais celui des services, mais c'est galement le cas des secteurs de l'nergie, notamment lectrique, des transports, notamment ferroviaires, ou encore des services postaux. 7 Ce chiffre sera actualis lors de la publication par Eurostat des statistiques 2004 (officiellement avant la fin du mois de mars). 25 C. Le dfi de l'largissement Dix nouveaux pays ont rejoint l'UE le 1er mai 2004. Ils ont vocation  adopter l'euro aprs avoir satisfait aux critres de convergence nominale. Au-del des dfis institutionnels qui subsistent (indpendance des banques centrales, adaptation de systmes bancaires, lutte contre le blanchiment, etc.), le dfi majeur qui s'ouvre  nous est de relever le pari de la convergence relle entre l'Est et l'Ouest de l'Europe. Cet objectif ncessitera des annes d'importantes rformes structurelles favorables  une acclration de la croissance et au comblement du foss Est-Ouest ; il suppose notamment le respect du cadre macroconomique auquel tous les Etats membres parties  l'euro aujourd'hui ont consenti, en particulier la participation russie au MCE II. Il faut en effet viter toute prcipitation dommageable  la comptitivit et procder aux rformes de fond, notamment en matire de soutenabilit des finances publiques, pralablement  l'entre dans ce mcanisme de change, gage d'une convergence relle durable profitable  l'ensemble de la zone. Conclusion  Je souhaiterais conclure en disant que l'euro a rpondu  nos attentes. Aprs le dfi sans prcdent du passage  l'euro fiduciaire  l'chelle du continent, qui a t couronn de succs, l'euro a remplac quasi-instantanment les anciennes monnaies nationales, sans perturbation logistique. Il a encourag la stabilit grce  la crdibilit dont il jouit et a protg nombre de pays de la zone contre la volatilit excessive des taux de change et les turbulences enregistres sur les marchs financiers. Ces rsultats doivent tre souligns avec d'autant plus d'insistance que pendant plusieurs annes il avait t dit que l'euro resterait un  serpent de mer  ou qu'il crerait des difficults macroconomiques importantes. Ces scnarios ne se sont pas concrtiss.  L'euro reprsente donc une pierre angulaire majeure de la construction europenne. Cela dit, et indpendamment de ses propres mrites, une monnaie ne constitue pas une fin en soi mme si les nouveaux tats membres sont ardemment dtermins  l'adopter le plus vite possible. La participation  l'union montaire doit reposer sur un processus de convergence soutenable. L'largissement de la zone euro donnera  cet gard un nouvel lan au relvement des dfis, les responsables de politique conomique subissant 26 dsormais une pression beaucoup plus forte dans le traitement des difficults alors qu'ils pouvaient les ignorer auparavant. Il s'agit l d'une contribution essentielle  la construction d'une union europenne plus forte  laquelle j'adhre vigoureusement. En conclusion, laissez-moi exprimer ma confiance en l'avenir de l'euro qui, six ans aprs sa cration, constitue le symbole patent de l'identit europenne et de sa force. 27

Title: Hearing of Franois Villeroy de Galhau, Governor of the Banque de France, before the Finance Committee and the European Affairs Committee of the National Assembly
Subtitle: Hearing of Franois Villeroy de Galhau, Governor of the Banque de France, before the Finance Committee and the European Affairs Committee of the National Assembly
text: Hearing of Francois Villeroy de Galhau, Governor of the Banque de France, before the Finance Committee and the European Affairs Committee of the National Assembly Paris, 6 May 2020 Press contacts: Mark Deen (mark.deen@banque-france.fr) and Deborah Guedj (deborah.guedj@banque-france.fr Page 1 sur 6 Mr President, Madam President, Mr Rapporteur-General, ladies and gentlemen, I would like to thank you for welcoming me this afternoon, virtually and exceptionally, before the two Committees. The Banque de France regularly "reports" to you, the elected representatives of the Nation, but this task is even more essential during this unprecedented crisis. I will begin with a few words on the economic situation; I will then address the strong mobilisation of the Banque de France and the ECB during the crisis, before outlining the conditions for economic recovery. I. The economic situation during the lockdown As regards the economic effects of the lockdown, we are converging towards a loss of activity of about one third. The figure for the first quarter published by INSEE last Thursday confirms this order of magnitude, in line with the -6% we had forecast as early as 8 April: -5.8% of GDP over three months corresponding to -32% over a fortnight in March. These effects will be mechanically more pronounced in the second quarter because they will be longer-lasting. We will estimate them for April in our next monthly business survey to be published on 12 May. However, it is still too early for us to forecast the recession in 2020 and the expected rebound in 2021. A word on the first comparison with other European economies, which should be taken with much caution: all have slowed significantly, but France more so than Germany; even Spain and Italy have seen their construction sector less affected than in France, and recourse to short-time work appears to be much stronger in our country, with the most generous compensation package. There may be several useful lessons to be learned for exiting the lockdown; it is essential for our economic health that France now returns to work at full capacity, while of course ensuring the protection of all employees. II. The mobilisation of the Banque de France and the ECB during the crisis Page 2 sur 6 During this crisis, the Banque de France immediately focused its activities on five key fronts: (i) supporting households in difficulty as well as VSEs and SMEs through the Banks network across France  I would like to stress the essential role played by Credit Mediation, under the aegis of the Banque de France, in each departement  the number of daily requests for mediation has reached 200, the vast majority of which are from VSEs: in one week, this figure is higher than in the whole of last year, but it is less than 1.5% of the requests for Stateguaranteed loans; (ii) responding to needs for cash  we have not experienced any supply problems; (iii) economic analysis and monetary policy; (iv) careful monitoring of the markets; (v) and supervision of the financial soundness of banks and insurance companies via the ACPR. We are also on the front line of the European response, that of the ECB Governing Council. It was rapid  within six days, as early as 12 and 18 March  and massive  in terms of potential liquidity for businesses and governments. And, so far, it has been effective in financing the sharp increase in corporate loans (7.5% in one year in France at end-March) and stabilising their cost. But, as we just said last Thursday, we will be as flexible as required  in particular to avoid the fragmentation of the euro area, with unjustified interest rate increases in some countries; and we will be as innovative as necessary regarding instruments. Our Governing Council took note yesterday of the judgement by the German Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe: as the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) has said, our past actions are indeed proportionate to our mandate, and our determination for the future to deliver on that mandate is total. Allow me to express a broader consideration, at a time when some voices are being raised in various quarters to call into question the independence of the central bank and its mandate focused on price stability. Criticising these two pillars seems to me not only unnecessary, but also dangerous. Unnecessary because the ECB has demonstrated its ability to innovate and to act swiftly while remaining within its mandate. But it is also dangerous because Page 3 sur 6 these two pillars, which are enshrined in the democratically voted Treaty, are the legal basis for our action. Even more so, they are the basis for Europeans' confidence in their currency. We cannot cancel the public debts we hold today, neither legally, nor from a fiduciary point of view: a suspicion of fiscal dominance would cause mistrust in the currency. Independence and price stability do in no way stand in the way of powerful action by the ECB, on the contrary. Our definition of price stability is an inflation rate below but close to 2% over the medium term, and this target is a symmetric target, not a ceiling. In comparison, inflation is currently low: it stands at 0.4% in the euro area and 0.5% in France; our estimate is that it should remain below 1% overall, contrary to the fears of our fellow citizens, who have seen a temporary rise in food prices. The current shock is disinflationary, with low oil prices and, more broadly, demand that is likely to recover more slowly than supply. And so, in the very name of our mandate, we will be able to go further, and we will most likely have to go further, and thus support the recovery through low interest rates and abundant liquidity for a long time. III. The conditions for a recovery: a triangle of reassurances Initial hopes were for a rapid V-shaped recovery. It is clear today that it will take time, and that, beyond the Act 1 emergency phase, patient and selective measures will be needed to guide the recovery. Getting back onto a better economic footing will require what I call a triangle of reassurances: household confidence, the solvency of businesses and the sustainability of public debt. 1/ Unfortunately, some households have been made more vulnerable by the crisis, and it is crucial that they be helped through solidarity. But on the whole, household consumption will have fallen to a much greater extent than household income during this lockdown, leading to a significant build-up of forced savings  at least EUR 15 billion in March, and probably EUR 60 billion by the end of May. Going forward, these reserves will need to be converted rapidly into spending and hence growth. To ensure economic confidence, it will Page 4 sur 6 be preferable in the short-term to avoid the recessionary impact of higher household taxes. More than purchasing power, therefore, the priority regarding households is their confidence. If a tax measure for all households were to be envisaged, it would be better to focus on temporary and targeted incentives to encourage households to consume their savings. 2/ For businesses and the self-employed, the exit from lockdown will potentially prove risky. Despite major liquidity support, the irrecoverable losses in revenue will have damaged their solvency. Their overall debt has already increased sharply, by 2% or EUR 32 billion in March alone. Support for businesses will therefore need to be redirected in part from the loans seen in Act 1 towards quasi-equity. But to avoid any windfall effects or ruinous failures, the scheme will have to be both efficient and selective. Act 1 was broadspread; the next acts will need to set priorities. Another idea would be to allow companies to offset their 2020 losses immediately against their corporation tax for 2019 and previous years. Those sectors subject to a longterm shutdown will have to be provided with ad-hoc support. Among other measures, the Ministry of the Economy has proposed injecting public capital into listed companies, provided they are viable. For SMEs, however, a system of crowdlending will be more appropriate. One interesting suggestion from several economists is that we should set up a temporary European business recapitalisation fund, which could be linked to the EIB. This would have the dual advantage of (i) levelling the playing field between countries, by ensuring that those least in debt today do not provide more help to their own national companies; and (ii) potentially bringing Northern and Southern Europe into agreement, so that we can end the somewhat sterile debate over loans and subsidies. 3/ The cushioning mechanism put in place by the government is playing a massive role, which is good news: it is absorbing around 60% of the current shock, with the balance mainly being absorbed by companies and, to a more Page 5 sur 6 marginal extent  around 5%  by employees. The price of this mechanism is that public debt will have increased by at least 17 percentage points to 115% of GDP by end-2020. The post-lockdown period will therefore be a delicate balancing act for public finances, between fostering a rapid recovery and ensuring long-term sustainability. Supporting the recovery could mean dealing with the debt inherited from the crisis separately, by partially ring-fencing it  the only advantage of which would be to push back its repayment further into the future. Conversely, for future debt associated with the financing of the recovery, the idea of pooling it with more financially sound countries was what inspired the post-war Marshall Plan. The French proposal for a common European fund to finance new investment programmes, for the climate for example, would be the best way of showing European solidarity. But there is no magic bullet: in the long run, this debt will need to be financed through growth and through our work  which is why a balance needs to be found in fiscal policy. It is up to the government and parliament to make the necessary adjustments, but I would just like to raise two points: - In the short run, it is normal  and even desirable  to have a high deficit, in order to counter the recession. But we need to prioritise spending that is temporary, and even reversible debt  such as investment in firms quasiequity  and avoid permanent spending or tax cuts which would place an unjustified burden on the post-crisis period. Again in the short run, we will need to avoid tightening fiscal policy too soon into the recovery. - Conversely, in the medium term, once growth is firmly established, we will need to come back to a more selective fiscal policy, and to more efficient public spending. This is the structural challenge that France faces, while at the same time prioritising investment in the future, which means in education, professional training and a more qualified workforce. In the four years from 2016 to 2019, we notched up some impressive collective successes in terms of employment; we will need to pick up where we left off. In this way, I hope we will be able to overcome this harsh challenge for our country. Page 6 sur 6 Thank you for your attention and I am happy to answer any questions.

Title: Central banks' dilemmas in the face of uncertainty
text: Speech by Mr Christian Noyer Governor of the Banque de France CENTRAL BANKS' DILEMMAS IN THE FACE OF UNCERTAINTY 5 JUNE 2006 BUENOS AIRES Ladies and gentlemen, 95 I would like to thank you for inviting me to participate in this seminar. It gives me great pleasure to speak on such an interesting topic, namely: "Central banks' dilemmas in the face of uncertainty". 95 In the first part of my speech, I will recall the nature of uncertainty and its importance for central banks; in the second part, I will summarize various proposals aimed at responding to this uncertainty. I/ The nature of uncertainty Uncertainty manifests itself in different forms. This is a key issue for central banks in general (I/1) and perhaps even more so for the Eurosystem (I/2). 1) The importance of uncertainty for central banks 95 The importance of risk and uncertainty for economic analysis was first mentioned by Frank Knight (Risk, Uncertainty and Profit) in 1921. "Risk" refers to situations in which the decision-maker can assign probabilities to the various events he or she is likely to face; "uncertainty" applies to situations where this randomness cannot be translated into probabilities. 95 Uncertainty is a key issue for central banks: according to Alan Greenspan, "uncertainty is not just an important part of monetary policy; it is the major characteristic of this environment." Therefore, I will focus on monetary policy, although the subject could also apply to financial stability, which is another major concern for central banks. 2) The Eurosystem is confronted with general but also specific sources of uncertainty 95 From a general point of view, uncertainties can be linked to: - macroeconomic indicators, which may be unobservable (output gap) or subject to revision (GDP); - the nature and degree of persistence of shocks: for example, shocks affecting oil and raw materials, the extent of their diffusion to prices, etc.; - the transmission of monetary policy to the real economy, Milton Friedman having shown that "monetary policy acts with long and variable delays"; - possible distortions of asset prices and wealth effects. 95 But in the case of the euro area, the uncertainty may be even greater: - the available time series are short; - the eurozone has potentially experienced a Lucas-style regime change; - the euro plays a catalytic role for structural change. II/ What attitude should be adopted in the face of uncertainty? The economic literature has proposed monetary policy guidelines (II/1) and various approaches (II/2) to address uncertainty. 1) Monetary policy guidelines has. Ignoring uncertainty 95 If uncertainty is related to data or shocks (so-called "additive" uncertainty), the optimal solution may be to make decisions as in an environment free of uncertainty. 95 In this case, according to the "certain equivalent principle" (Poole, 1970), monetary policy must react to the best estimation of variables exactly as it would in the presence of perfectly measured variables. b. Caution 95 This approach was popularized by Brainard: "parametric" uncertainty calls for caution in responding to economic disruptions, which argues for a gradual approach (Brainard, 1967). In addition, the uncertainty associated with the "long and variable transmission times of monetary policy," dear to Milton Friedman, militates against attempts to "fine-tune" the economy through monetary policy interventions. 95 In addition, the central bank should not adjust its monetary policy solely to meet market expectations1: - capital markets behave in a mimetic manner while central banks are cautious; - markets are sensitive to speculative bubbles while central banks focus on fundamentals; - the orientation of the markets is short-term while that of central banks is medium- and long-term. 95 However, sometimes market decisions are wrong when monetary policy does not match their expectations. The central bank must therefore be intertemporally consistent. The usual approach, in such a context, is to make a gradual change in the policy rate. 95 From a practical point of view, the step-by-step approach has many advantages: 1 A. Blinder (1998) - it reduces the risk of having to take monetary policy decisions quickly, reversing previous decisions; - it reduces the likelihood of disruptions on the capital markets; - it is particularly suitable for major risks. Debate on possible differences in the behaviour of the Eurosystem and the Fed in terms of gradualism 95 The fact that the euro area appeared to have behaved less actively than the Fed in reducing interest rates after 2001 and that these rates remained stable over an extended period between June 2003 and December 2005 raised the following question: Is the Eurosystem "too passive"? 95 Activism and gradualism are measured by the number and magnitude of changes in the policy rate over a given period. 95 Recent studies based on an estimated model for the euro area and the United States over the past two decades have led to the following three conclusions2: - there are indeed differences in the monetary policy strategies implemented by the Eurosystem and the Fed; - the degree of smoothing of interest rates, considered an indicator of monetary gradualism, is quite similar in the euro area and in the United States; - differences in development patterns can be attributed to shocks of a dissimilar nature and magnitude, with demand shocks having for example been larger in the United States, thus calling for a stronger monetary policy response. 2 Motto and Rostagno (2005) and Sahuc and Smets (2006) Monetary policy and asset prices 95 Prudence is also an appropriate answer to the question: Should monetary policy respond systematically to perceived distortions in asset prices? Three factors of uncertainty must be taken into account: - first, the assessment of these distortions is, in essence, surrounded by a high degree of uncertainty, linked to the determination of the equilibrium prices of assets and the nature of the transmission to the real economy; - second, central banks must ensure that the risks to the economy are balanced: a monetary policy measure aimed at reducing the risk of suffering a significant loss in the future could prove very costly in the short term; - thirdly, the impact of monetary policy decisions on asset prices is highly uncertain. 95 The announcement of a systematic response could therefore lead to an intensification of moral hazard and damage the credibility of the central bank in the fight against inflation, a credibility that is its most valuable asset. Moreover, the single interest rate instrument cannot be directed simultaneously on two potentially contradictory objectives. There are two cases in which gradualism should not be systematically adopted: 95 First, the best way to prevent the worst-case scenario may be to follow rather aggressive monetary policy rules to reduce the deviations of inflation from the target set. 95 Second, a more activist rule is likely to generate more information, which improves the amount of knowledge gained by the central bank and thus its subsequent monetary policy performance. Nevertheless, this The learning process can be costly as it can lead to increased economic volatility. 2) Some approaches to dealing with uncertainty a) Rely on monetary policy rules Simple monetary policy rules (such as Taylor's rule) can work well for a range of models. A rule-based approach also has the advantage of providing greater predictability to policy, which facilitates the formation of expectations. - However, if followed systematically, a rule may not take into account relevant information on risks to price stability. On the other hand, a disadvantage of the rules defined too narrowly is their inability to provide a real solution to complex problems. b) Pay attention to "distribution tail" events - The concern to maintain the stability of the financial system and to contain the systemic risk that may affect the capital markets is at the heart of the central bank's mission. In a market-based system, it is essential that all operators focus on sound risk management to guard against the danger of a financial crisis linked to a low-probability event (tail of distribution). These practices enhance financial stability without increasing moral hazard. Operators familiar with risk indicators, stress test methodologies (and associated scenarios) will be more likely to continue to provide access to credit in times of systemic and institutional crisis. - Stress tests use either historical data from asset price distributions or hypothetical scenarios that provide insights into the financial risks associated with investment and hedging strategies. Focusing market operators' attention on crisis structures could help limit the impact of a distribution tail event of low probability but particularly high cost. * * * I will conclude by explaining why I believe that the Eurosystem, with its policy framework, is able to deal with different types of uncertainties. - First, the Eurosystem takes into account the uncertainty associated with transmission hazards in the medium-term stance of its monetary policy strategy. It introduces flexibility into the decision-making process and avoids focusing on short-term developments. The choice of medium-term horizon is also a way to reconcile monetary policy and financial stability considerations, allowing the central bank to "see beyond the bubble". - Secondly, the Eurosystem does not rely on a single model for the inflationary process. The two-pillar approach based on a dual analysis, economic and monetary, provides additional information on the determinants of short and medium term inflation (economic analysis) and longer-term inflation (monetary analysis). Economic analysis is based on a wide range of economic, short-term and financial indicators (real economy data and soft data) as well as forecasts (Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projection exercises assessed in parallel with other institutions' forecasts). Monetary analysis is based on a comprehensive assessment of liquidity and credit conditions. These two analyses can be cross-checked to provide an overall assessment of the risks to price stability over the medium term. Alternative models of the inflation process justify the Eurosystem's comprehensive information-based approach to overcoming uncertainty. In a way, the two-pillar approach is based on the same principles as the treatment of uncertainty in a Bayesian Model Averaging, but it is less formal. Thirdly, the higher the uncertainty, the more transparency is needed and the greater the credibility. The Eurosystem has managed to anchor inflation expectations at a level very close to its target, reflecting a high level of credibility. Despite high and rising oil prices, inflation expectations (as measured by inflation breakevens from indexed bonds) have remained stable at around 2% since the beginning of 2006. Credibility, which anchors inflation expectations, helps reduce uncertainty about future developments and stabilize the economy. This makes it easier for economic agents to understand short-term interest rate decisions and the long-term central bank's reaction function.

Title: Over-indebtedness and civil bankruptcy how to prevent
text: Colloquium "Solidarity: a financial value?" National Assembly Wednesday, 22 June 2005 --------- Round table Nb04: "Over-indebtedness and civil bankruptcy: how to prevent?" Introductory statement by Christian NOYER, Governor of the Banque de France The Governor of the Bank of France can only be concerned about the subject of this round table, and this in two ways. This is the case, first of all, because it is the very task of any central bank, and therefore of the Bank of France within the ESCB, to ensure, at macroeconomic level, an optimal allocation of credit, both in quantity and quality. Preventing the excessive distribution of credit is an integral part of our role as monetary authority. Ensuring the overall control of credit risks is part of the prudential responsibilities of the Banking Commission, of which the Banque de France provides the General Secretariat. But, and this is a French particularity, the Banque de France is interested in another way in the prevention of over-indebtedness of households, since the legislator has entrusted it for more than fifteen years, the specific mission of providing the secretariat of the commissions of over-indebtedness of individuals whose role is to try to find, either through negotiation with creditors or in cooperation with the judicial authority, solutions to the repayment problems encountered by over-indebted households. The accomplishment of this mission represents a significant burden for the Bank of France since it mobilizes about 20% of the staff of its Network (more than 1300 EATP in the recently past period). We strive to accomplish it as best we can, with maximum concern for efficiency in the interest of the over-indebted but also of the national community which ultimately bears the costs related to the exercise of this mission. For these two sets of reasons, the Banque de France can only take a keen interest in the prevention of over-indebtedness and contribute to it to the extent of its possibilities. But, before addressing the problem of prevention, it seems to me essential, given the conclusions we have drawn from the observation of this phenomenon and its evolution, to clearly define what we want to prevent in order to look for the most appropriate devices. This implies clearly identifying the notion of over-indebtedness itself (I) before questioning its prevention (II). I. What is over-indebtedness? A) Originally..... Thus posed, after fifteen years of dealing with the phenomenon, several legislative interventions and many debates on the subject, the question may, at first glance, appear surprising. The fact remains that the reality covered by this term has profoundly evolved since the beginning and that there are probably several notions of "over-indebtedness" Admittedly, by defining, in 1990, that concept as 'the manifest impossibility for the debtor in good faith to meet all his non-professional debts due and to expire", the legislator adopted a generic definition broad enough to cover a wide range of situations and this definition has therefore been able to remain unchanged to date. It is nevertheless clear, both on reading the reasons for that law and on examination of its provisions, that it was intended to respond to a certain type of situation, characterised by the difficulty of repaying loans contracted with bodies belonging to the banking and financial sphere (which probably justified the choice to entrust the Banque de France with the role then assigned to it). The years immediately preceding the adoption of the law had, in fact, been marked by a sharp increase in household debt for the acquisition of real estate, often by means of loans with progressive maturities subscribed, counting on the continuation of the inflationary trends observed previously to reduce the repayment burden. At the same time, consumer credit had experienced an unprecedented quantitative boom in our country and took on new, more modern forms such as lease with option to purchase, particularly in the automotive sector, or revolving credit, consisting of a reserve of purchasing power that could be replenished as repayments were made. In some years, the rate of growth of outstanding loans has been around 30 or even 40%. It was at this time that the phenomenon known as "debt spirals" developed, consisting in taking out new loans to repay the old ones, a phenomenon that led, almost inexorably, to an inability to repay. In this context, "over-indebtedness" was the consequence of a "financial bubble" and the main objective of the law was to help a relatively limited number of borrowers in difficulty (estimated at 200,000) to honour their commitments by adjusting the repayment terms by combining conventional solutions in this area (interest rate reduction, deferrals and rescheduling, etc.). B) Since the mid-1990s Since the years 1995-1996, there has been an uninterrupted year-on-year increase in the number of applications filed with over-indebtedness commissions: from 70,000 in 1995, the number of these annual filings rose to 118,000 in 1998, to 148,000 in 2000, and then, after a slight decrease in 2001 and 2002, to 166,000 in 2003 and 188,000 in 2004. From these developments and the observations to which they have given rise, two conclusions can be drawn. - 1) First of all, the phenomenon of household over-indebtedness, provisionally estimated in 1990, has become permanent; it appears quite often disconnected from the economic situation. We can think in this regard that the significant media coverage to which over-indebtedness has been subject (on the occasion of the various reforms affecting its treatment, a peak of deposits has been observed), the improvement of the knowledge of existing devices by individuals and social relays have contributed to deeply inscribe these devices in our environment. - 2) Secondly, the profile of over-indebted debtors has changed considerably since 1990; over-indebted people described as "liabilities", i.e. those who had satisfactory repayment capacities when they went into debt but saw these subsequently reduced due to an accident in their lives (loss of employment, illness, divorce, etc.), which already existed in 1990, are now largely in the majority (nearly two-thirds of deposits). (3) Finally, debtors whose situation was characterized by low resources to meet the commission counters to enable them to cope very well. difficult to the expenses of everyday life and whose liabilities were essentially composed of arrears of these expenses to which were added some bank debts of small amount in the form of overdrafts or revolving credits. Faced with such situations, the commissions could not apply conventional financial solutions and could only propose successive moratoriums on all debts that eventually led to new filings of files. It is thus apparent from a typological survey carried out by the Bank in 2001 that: - 27% of the filings came from households with no repayment capacity, - in the same vein, 30% of the cases were redeposits, either at the end of a moratorium or because of a change in situation that occurred during the implementation of a recovery plan, - finally, the low income, often less than 1500 euros and frequently below the SMIC, often combined with a few revolving loans or a small bank overdraft, revealed the existence of a recourse to credit more suffered than desired, making the financial situation of the household vulnerable to the slightest alea. The legislator drew the consequences of these developments by adapting the methods of treatment, first in 1998 and then, more radically, in 2003 by instituting the personal recovery procedure. At present, several modes of treatment of over-indebtedness coexist, adapted to the diversity of situations. As well, the evolutionary and protean nature of the phenomenon leads us to question the existing or conceivable prevention device(s). II. What prevention? The previous developments tend to consider that there is no single device to prevent all forms of over-indebtedness. It is therefore simply possible, as an introduction to this debate, to outline or recall some ideas. From a macroeconomic point of view, it is first necessary - and this is of particular interest to the monetary authorities and the professionals concerned - to be unfailingly vigilant and to be careful not to believe that over-indebtedness phenomena of the type observed in 1990 are definitively over. The nation's financial accounts in 2004, which show a strong annual increase in household debt in the form of short- and especially long-term loans, can only raise certain questions. Admittedly, the indebtedness of resident households in relation to Gross Domestic Product still appears to be lower than that observed in the euro zone as a whole, in the United Kingdom or the United States, but it is now at a level not seen since the period before the bursting of the housing bubble in the early 1990s. The general context is obviously not at all the same, but our current concern is not so much the result of the level of household debt as of its growth, which not only remains significant but above all is increasing (the increase in outstanding amounts from one year to the next reached 8.9% in 2004 after growth of 7% in 2003 and 6.4% in 2002). To ensure concrete prevention, two ways have been favoured both in France and in foreign countries. Has. Working with files In our country, professionals have, in addition to their own decision support tools such as scores or expert systems, the possibility of accessing information on borrower defaults that is contained in the File of Incidents of repayment of loans to Individuals (known by the initials FICP) managed by the Bank of France. The preventive nature of this file, now accessible in real time via the INTERNET, has recently been reinforced by a crbf regulation (Nb02004-01) which lowered the reporting thresholds. Thus, the characterized payment incidents to be declared to the file are now, in the most frequent case, namely that of monthly repayable credits, those have the amount reached at least double (instead of triple previously) of the last due date; by schematizing, it means that a defaulting borrower is now filed from the second default and no longer from the third. Information relating to situations of over-indebtedness is also listed in this file: since 2004, filers have been identified as early as possible, that is to say as soon as the referral to the over-indebtedness commission without waiting, as before, for the file to have been declared admissible by the latter. Without legally hindering the granting of credit, a registration in the FICP constitutes a serious alert as to the willingness or ability of a candidate borrower to repay his debts and should normally encourage caution the institution that consults this file, in which are currently registered 2.2 million people. In practice, consultation of the FICP, although legally optional, is almost systematic before an institution grants credit. This preventive device also includes the Central Register of Cheques whose operating principles are different, which also lists 2 million people prohibited from issuing cheques, which can also be consulted in real time on the INTERNET and which can be questioned, not only as part of the "cheque policy" but also before the granting of credit. Should we go further in this area and set up a positive file listing all the appropriations granted? This subject alone deserves a long debate. Proponents of this solution, which has been adopted by some European countries, argue that such a tool would allow lenders to better understand the state of indebtedness of a potential borrower and therefore to grant new credit only wisely, under penalty of incurring their responsibility. Others argue, on the other hand, that this solution, which would involve filing about twelve million households, would have a cost disproportionate to its advantages, especially since it would not prevent passive over-indebtedness, which is now in the majority. Moreover, in order to ensure its effectiveness, should we not identify all debts, whatever their nature and origin? (including tax liabilities, rent arrears...)? Should we only track credit authorizations or also track uses in real time, which would be much more complex? Beyond these relatively technical considerations, this "track" raises questions that are more of an ethical or political choice, with regard to the protection of privacy, the risk of exclusion of some, in particular the most disadvantaged households, from the official credit circuits, and finally the possibility of misuse of the purpose of such a file for canvassing purposes. All these questions deserve, at the very least, to be seriously studied, in the light, in particular, of foreign experiences. B. Borrower protection Effective prevention also requires a system of protection and information for borrowers to prevent them from making commitments without measuring all the consequences. This concern is relatively old in our country. As early as 1978, the so-called Scrivener law concerning consumer credit established for the benefit of the borrower a right of withdrawal allowing him to revoke within seven days a consent that he would have given too hastily to a movable credit transaction. In 1979, another Scrivener law instituted a minimum reflection period of ten clear days before the acceptance of a mortgage. At the beginning of the decade that began in 1990, the Neiertz Law, at the same time as it created the mechanism for dealing with over-indebtedness, modified the legal regime of the permanent credit offer, in particular by limiting its validity to a renewable period of one year and by obliging the lender to indicate to the borrower, three months before the maturity, the conditions for renewing the contract and to propose to the latter (when the latter does not wish to renew the credit) a staggered repayment. At the beginning of the current decade, the so-called MURCEF law of 11 December 2001 and the financial security law of 1 August 2003 intervened, on the one hand, to regulate advertising in terms of consumer credit, on the other hand, to strengthen the information of the borrower during the period of execution of a revolving credit: thus, he must now receive monthly, and within a "reasonable time" before the date of payment, an updated and detailed statement of the performance of his contract including certain information listed by law. Very recently, this legislative environment has, once again, been enriched with the so-called Che2tel law of 28 January 2005 which has in particular further increased the information to be given to the borrower, allowed the termination at any time by the latter of a revolving credit agreement, subject to compliance with the repayment conditions, and provided that in the event of non-use of the credit for three years, the lender must propose in writing the renewal of the contract to the borrower, whose lack of response leads to the termination of the contract. Finally, among these interventions of the legislator "lato sensu", we can not fail to mention the draft European directive on the harmonization of legislation on consumer credit. A second draft is being drawn up after the failure of a first one and it is likely that this approach will eventually lead to a Community text. Before concluding, I would also like to point out that one of the most important factors of prevention lies in the approach, which has already been largely undertaken by the institutions, under the impetus and with the encouragement of the supervisory authorities, in order to better select their clientele and better control their risks. These efforts must, of course, be continued relentlessly and I believe that all professionals have understood this. What to conclude? Our country is already probably the one with the most dense legislation in the field of prevention and treatment of over-indebtedness. Despite the situations that continue to be observed, this legislation has certainly helped to moralize the market and improve its transparency. Faced with the heterogeneity and evolutionary nature of the phenomenon, should we continue to seek solutions to all cases through legislation, at the risk of leading to a stratification of the texts that is ultimately harmful to their readability? On the other hand, should we not deepen some of the avenues already explored, for example by relying on the self-discipline of professionals, on the search for greater consultation between them and consumer organisations which are close to the field and are undoubtedly the best able to negotiate improvements that are really adapted to the reality they face on a daily basis? Should we not, also as close as possible to the field, encourage active pedagogy vis-e0-vis consumers who are often insufficiently informed about the mechanisms of credit, as well as the laws that govern them? Finally, in the most difficult cases, would not the solution lie in strengthening social support, both for the prevention and treatment of over-indebtedness? These are the few avenues that I wanted, at the end of this introduction, to give to your reflection.

Enfin, parmi ces interventions du lgislateur  lato sensu , on ne peut manquer dvoquer le projet de directive europenne dharmonisation des lgislations sur le crdit  la consommation. Un second projet est en cours dlaboration aprs lchec dun premier et il est probable que cette dmarche finira par dboucher sur un texte communautaire. Avant de conclure, je tiens galement  souligner que lun des facteurs les plus importants de prvention rside dans la dmarche, qui a dj t largement engage par les tablissements, sous limpulsion et avec lencouragement des autorits de contrle, en vue de mieux slectionner leur clientle et de mieux matriser leurs risques. Ces efforts doivent naturellement tre poursuivis sans relche et je crois que tous les professionnels lont bien compris Que conclure ? Notre pays est, dores et dj, probablement celui qui sest dot de la lgislation la plus dense dans le domaine de la prvention et du traitement du surendettement. En dpit des situations que lon continue dobserver, cette lgislation a certainement contribu  moraliser le march et  amliorer sa transparence. Face  lhtrognit et au caractre volutif du phnomne, faut-il continuer  rechercher par la voie lgislative des solutions  tous les cas, au risque daboutir  une stratification des textes finalement nuisible  leur lisibilit ? Ne doit-on pas, en revanche, approfondir quelques voies dj explores, par exemple en comptant sur lautodiscipline des professionnels, sur la recherche dune plus grande concertation entre ceux-ci et les organisations de consommateurs qui sont proches du terrain et sont sans doute les mieux  mme de ngocier des amliorations rellement adaptes  la ralit  laquelle elles sont quotidiennement confrontes. Ne faut-il pas, galement au plus prs du terrain, encourager une pdagogie active vis--vis des consommateurs qui sont souvent insuffisamment informs des mcanismes du crdit, ainsi dailleurs que des lois qui les rgissent. Enfin, dans les cas les plus difficiles, la solution ne rsiderait-elle pas dans un renforcement de laccompagnement social, tant pour la prvention que pour le traitement du surendettement ? Telles sont les quelques pistes que je voulais, en conclusion de cette introduction, livrer  votre rflexion.

Title: Presentation of the Annual report
text: PRESENTATION OF THE BANKING COMMISSION'S ANNUAL REPORT FOR 2004 Christian Noyer, Governor of the Banque de France, President of the Banking Commission The Banking Commission's Annual Report for 2004 is published today. On the basis of its content, I would like to insist to you on three important axes of the recent and upcoming developments of the French banking system: - the results of French credit institutions were very good in 2004; - there are significant risks to the sustainability of those performances; - ongoing regulatory changes should help to improve the risk management. 1. THE RESULTS OF FRENCH CREDIT INSTITUTIONS WERE FAVOURABLE IN 2004 On the basis of their social accounts, the net result of all credit institutions increased by almost 30% over the last financial year to 8022.5 billion. The evolution of the consolidated net income of the seven main groups was almost as strong, with an increase of 24%. This remarkable increase, also observed in the France's neighbouring countries, was based on a particular combination of relatively favourable economic and financial factors. 1 1.1. Banking performance in France 2004 is mainly due to the fall in provision account allocations French credit institutions, like their European counterparts, benefited from global growth and, in France, sustained internal consumption. The net banking income (GNP) of all French credit institutions grew by 4.8%, but was lower than in 2003 when it reached more than 7%. Retail banking activities were particularly dynamic, accounting for more than half of GNP in the main groups, performance in asset management was better than before as well as in the corporate and investment banking sector. Overheads recorded a fairly significant increase, of the order of 4% for all credit institutions. In total, operating ratios improved slightly on a social basis to 63.9% from 64.4%. However, France remains slightly above the European average on the basis of a comparison of the main banking groups, at 64.5% against a European average of 61.8%. Finally, and this is the main explanation for the improvement in the net profitability of French banks, the immediate accounting cost of risk, consisting mainly of net allocations to provisions on bad loans, has been reduced, in flow, by nearly 40% from one year to the next for the French banking system as a whole. At the same time, provisions for risks and charges, which are used to cover less precisely identified risks, have given rise to a few net increases. 2 The provisioning effort accounted for just over 1 per cent of net banking income, up from more than 11 per cent in 1998. 1.2. These good results are the result of a temporary combination of favourable factors Global growth reached more than 5 per cent in 2004, supported by high growth rates in the United States and Asia. Growth in the euro area has recovered to a pace of around 2%. French growth was slightly higher (2.3%), supported by household consumption. The situation of large companies has improved on both sides of the Atlantic, as shown by the decline in corporate insolvencies, rating upgrades and the significant, if not excessive, general decline in risk premia on debt securities and credit derivatives. Similarly, the improvement in the economic situation of the main emerging countries was reflected in the appreciation of their debts. Macroeconomic and financial conditions are, however, marked by rising uncertainties, linked to the rise in commodity prices and oil prices, which may have a negative impact on the financial situation of certain sectors (air transport, tourism, chemicals). Stock markets rose moderately in 2004, with the CAC 40 rising only 7.4 per cent, compared with 16 per cent in 2003. Financial markets have been marked by very low levels of interest rates, which have fostered low market price volatility and the formation of abundant liquidity. Finally, the intermediation activity of French credit institutions was again supported by the strong demand for loans from individuals, particularly to finance the acquisition of housing. The increase in outstanding loans to the 3 Customers in the metropolitan area thus reached 8.5% in 2004, as a result of the growth in outstanding housing loans, the amount of which increased by 12.8%, after rates of 8.3% in 2002 and 11.3% in 2003. Note the recovery in loans to businesses (non-financial corporations and individual entrepreneurs), which saw their outstanding amount increase by 6.9% after a decline of 2.8% a year earlier. 2. THERE ARE SIGNIFICANT RISKS TO THE SUSTAINABILITY OF THESE PERFORMANCES AND REQUIRE INCREASED VIGILANCE 2.1. The risks are already present The apparent low level of financial risks in 2004 should not be an illusion. This situation will not last, as certain signs or factors of analysis suggest. Many major international banks, including the French, have had to face a decline in their margins in several activities, given the sharp reduction in volatility in the markets and the decline in risk premia ("spreads"). The lower return on risk-taking has therefore led to a significant increase in volumes, particularly on riskier counterparties. In financial markets, spreads appear to be excessively low and do not adequately remunerate the underlying risks. The sharp variation in the prices of certain financial instruments due to individual downgrades in ratings observed in the 1st quarter of 2005 clearly shows the strong sensitivity of the markets to any cyclical deterioration, which could lead to significant losses for participants who have taken significant positions in them. 4 In retail banking, fierce competition encourages credit institutions to increase their market shares and thus the volumes of transactions to the detriment of the prices charged. The production of loans is thus accompanied by a deterioration in intermediation margins, particularly on housing financing. This activity has so far presented a low risk of late or non-repayment by debtors. However, in view of the volumes involved and the lengthening of the duration of loans, the deterioration in the quality of their management, in particular the relaxation, which the Banking Commission regrets to note at present, of the conditions for granting loans, may have negative effects in the future on the solvency of households and on the financial situation of banks. Greater rigour would therefore seem to me to be necessary in this area. I invite you to refer to the more detailed figures and comments contained in the study on "housing loans" published in the appendix to the Annual Report. This trend towards deteriorating margins is also observed on corporate financing, for which the credit risk is higher, which therefore requires more than ever the maintenance or even improvement of the selection mechanisms in force, regardless of the size of the borrowing company. In this context, the sharp decline in the provisioning effort, which continues at the beginning of 2005, is not a good sign because it leads to a weakening of the financial safety margins of credit institutions. This is why the maintenance or even the strengthening of the general provisions made by French credit institutions is fully justified in order to cope with a possible decline in the quality of counterparties which, as the past has already shown, can occur extremely quickly. Their amount must correspond to the coverage of the risks probabilized over a sufficiently long period to take into account the fluctuations in the cycles of the activities concerned. 5 Another point of attention for the banking supervisory authorities is the evolution of the level of capital which, despite the good results achieved by French banks in 2004, has not increased, the preference being implicitly given to the search for immediate return for shareholders appreciated in particular through the "return on equity". This trend has contributed to the reduction in the Core Capital Ratio (Tier 1) of several of the major French institutions. As it is important not to weaken the financial structure or put at risk the medium- and long-term profitability of credit institutions throughout the economic cycle, I invite banking leaders to take advantage of the current situation to maintain a good financial base of their Houses. 2.2. Prudent management must be sought more than ever In the current context, I would like to recall a principle to which banking supervisors are particularly attached: banking activities and risks must be managed over a medium- and long-term horizon. In this respect, the restoration of margins and guarantees on intermediation activities seems to me to be unavoidable. Thus, it is a matter of concern that large-scale developed financing operations such as housing loans are carried out at interest rates so low that they barely cover production costs and freeze the rate structure of assets for many years. In this context, the conditions for granting new loans and taking guarantees, contrary to the current trend, must be strict. A cautious stance towards counterparties that are notoriously risky due to the uncertain nature of their future results is even more necessary. It is crucial that credit institutions that engage with such counterparties, I am thinking in particular of hedge funds, put in place from the outset a specific and in-depth analysis of the risks induced by these operations, bearing in mind the criteria for diversifying individual, sectoral and 6 Geographical. Precautionary measures need to be strengthened when dealing with new, complex transactions in little-known and low-liquidity segments. Internal risk monitoring by banks and the vigilance of managers are essential in this regard. 3. REGULATORY DEVELOPMENTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO IMPROVING THE ORGANISATION AND EFFECTIVENESS OF RISK MANAGEMENT FOR CREDIT INSTITUTIONS AND INVESTMENT FIRMS 3.1. The Internal Control Regulation has been amended to allow for the most recent risk developments to be taken into account The level of quality of the internal control system is now a determining factor in the resilience of credit institutions and investment firms. Indeed, the ability of institutions to cope with changes in their environment depends largely on the organization of decision-making power and the security of internal processes. The France has just modernised, at the instigation of the Banking Commission, its regulations on the internal supervision of credit institutions and investment firms. This text, published on 31 March 2005, specifies the principles that should govern the establishment of the compliance control function and the monitoring of the risks associated with the subcontracting of activities. The establishment of an independent entity responsible for compliance monitoring must be accompanied by adequate human and technical resources as well as an exhaustive definition of its field of investigation. In general, these measures aim at better control by credit institutions and investment firms of the inherent financial, legal and reputational costs. 7 at these risks. Therefore, the Banking Commission will pay particular attention to the proper application of these provisions. 3.2. French credit institutions will meet the conditions for implementing the future solvency measurement system The Basel Committee published its outcome document in June 2004 setting out the new framework for the solvency of banks and in May 2005 clarified certain provisions relating in particular to the trading book. At the same time, on 14 July 2004, the European Commission published a first draft of the so-called CRD (Capital Requirements Directive), based on the Basel document. Discussions on the text have continued since then with a view to its adoption in 2005. To be ready to apply the new rules, institutions that have chosen advanced approaches to the measurement of credit and operational risks need to put in place internal measurement systems as soon as possible for recognition by supervisory authorities of their use for regulatory purposes. In the coming months, the Banking Commission will carry out an on-the-spot examination of the measures thus established to verify their compliance with the conditions laid down by the Basel Committee. Annexed to this report is a study on the "role of supervisors in the assessment of internal credit rating systems". 3.3. The entry into force of international accounting standards requires an adaptation of accounting management and financial reporting arrangements IAS/IFRS standards have been applicable in Europe since 1 January 2005 to the consolidated accounts of listed groups, including the main French banking groups. 8 The new accounting standards must be applied rigorously and consistently with prudential rules and good management practices. The Banking Commission will continue to base its supervisory tasks on banking groups on the examination of the accounting documents thus drawn up and of prudential statements that will take into account these new standards. However, in line with the recommendations of the Basel Committee and the Committee of European Banking Supervisors, in the preparation of which the Banking Commission and its Secretariat-General have been heavily involved, the accounting documents submitted to national authorities will have to include specific treatments designed to meet the objectives of prudential supervision. IAS/IFRS contain aspects that appear inadequate from the point of view of financial safety and stability, such as the provision that an undertaking's own funds increase as a result of the deterioration in the market's perception of its general financial situation. On 31 May 2005, the Banking Commission adopted an instruction setting out these prudential treatments and published as an annex to its Annual Report a specific study entitled "What prudential treatment for international accounting standards?". 3.4. The arrangements for informing banking supervisors will be adapted accordingly, in the context of European harmonisation Banking supervisors in Europe have undertaken to develop the documents submitted by credit institutions to them to take account of ongoing prudential and accounting regulatory changes. The work carried out in the most recent European Committee of Banking Supervisors has already led to the harmonisation of national practices in these areas, with the aim of the consistent application, within the European Economic Area, of the European Directive "CRD" and the strengthening of the convergence of the prudential practices of the Member States. In particular, it was decided to establish a harmonized arrangement 9 information both in the prudential field (Common Reporting, COREP) and in the accounting field (Financial Reporting, FINREP). Such an evolution meets several objectives: - reduce the management burden of credit institutions operating in several European countries by reducing country-specific information formats; - improve the regulatory equal treatment of banking players in the European Union; - modernise the transmission of data between supervised institutions and their authorities using the latest management and financial reporting techniques. It is important that French credit institutions integrate this new system as soon as possible, in close coordination with the Banking Commission. For its part, the Commission will mobilize all the means at its disposal to ensure that these new information methods are put in place at the right time. In the area of financial stability, the Banking Supervision Committee, which brings together bank supervisors and the national central banks of the ESCB within the ECB, continued its work on monitoring cyclical and structural developments in the European financial system, extending it to other areas of the financial sector, such as insurance or financial markets. All this numerous and intense work, which is developing at European level, aims to promote ever more dialogue, cooperation and the practical harmonisation of supervisory practices between the 25 countries of the Union. The current institutional framework, which rests on two legs, one national and the other European, demonstrated in 2005 its ability to implement common standards. 10 the implementation and supervision of the Basel II reform and IAS/IFRS. It has thus confirmed its solidity and adaptability. * * * * * To sum up and conclude, I would say that French credit institutions and investment firms performed well at the end of the 2004 financial year, but must give more priority to prudent management methods based on a long-term vision. The establishment of new prudential arrangements, including of a qualitative nature, must be a powerful and rapid factor in making progress in this regard. But it is also important for banks to strengthen their own vigilance and prudence in the various areas I have mentioned. It is in these conditions that the French banking centre, which is now undeniably solid and efficient, will maintain its international position and pursue its domestic and global development. 11
