Title: Tribune in Le Monde
text: Op-ed by Christian Noyer, Governor of the Banque de France published in Le Monde - February 12, 2014 "Let's preserve business financing" The European Commission has recently put forward proposals on the separation of market activities within banks. I have expressed strong reservations about this. My words may have been surprising. The Governor of the Bank of France chairs the Banking Supervisory Authority (ACPR). How can it oppose an initiative that aims to reduce risks, protect the taxpayer, and combat excessive and dangerous concentration of banking activities? The objective pursued by the Commission is legitimate, but the arrangements adopted are dangerous because they directly affect the financing of companies. His proposals stem from a false vision, according to which there are on the one hand the banks that make credit and on the other the financial markets that concentrate unnecessary risks to the economy. This is no longer the case today. The crisis has taught us, on the contrary, that finance forms a whole. Banks and markets are constantly interacting in financing companies of all sizes. This is true in times of crisis; this is also true in more normal times. This complementarity between banks and markets will be even more necessary in the future than in the past. Companies will always need banks, either for conventional loans or to raise funds from investors. But the new prudential requirements - which strengthen the soundness of banks - will also lead to a more selective distribution of credit. It is desirable that companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises, should be able to issue shares and bonds and find financing on the markets and from banks. The development of sound securitisation - through transparent, simple, homogeneous, regulated and supervised instruments - should help this powerfully. Banks must also be able to call on the major intermediaries who manage the savings of the French. And investors, individuals, small mutuals, supplementary pension funds, SICAV managers, will have to find banks capable of ensuring the liquidity of their investments. A healthy economy therefore depends on stable, robust and controlled relationships between banks, companies, insurance companies, pension funds and UCITS. That is, in deep, liquid, functional and well-regulated financial markets. To want to isolate themselves completely from each other is to slow down the financing of companies, to curb investment, to penalize savings and to reduce growth. The separation of activities, including in the form of subsidiaryisation, as proposed by the European Commission would probably lead to very serious financing difficulties for our companies. For example, market making by banks is not a highly remunerative activity. If it disappears, which investors will agree to buy corporate bonds without the prospect of being able to resell them easily if necessary? The state itself would be severely affected for the issuance of its debt. Similarly, the resources raised, without the help of its parent company, by a specialized subsidiary, will be limited and very expensive. I do not believe, under these conditions, that banks could continue to provide the same service, and at the same cost, to mid-caps and SMEs. I do not think that they could provide the same support to our companies in exporting, by managing in the same relationship with companies, their needs for credits of all kinds, their foreign exchange operations, their refinancing needs on the markets. It is an illusion, moreover, to think that a total specialization of banks through the separation of activities would strengthen security. Our experience is the opposite. During the crisis, the biggest bank losses occurred in highly specialized banks. Lehman Brothers was a pure investment bank, as was Bear Stearns. Northern Rock, which was the finest example of a bank run, was a pure retail bank. In contrast, the large universal banks, which are therefore diversified, have been more resilient to shocks. Over the past five years, the international community, under the aegis of the G20, has made great strides in regulating financial activities. European Commissioner Michel Barnier has played an important part in this - and I would like to pay tribute to him here very sincerely. The strengthening of banks' capital, which is particularly strong for large so-called systemic banks, the imposition of liquidity requirements, the establishment of resolution systems, the development of strengthened and more rigorous supervision, are major advances. In this new prudential landscape, regulation of market activities has its place. It is legitimate, in particular, to prohibit a bank from taking directional positions on its own account. This is the object, in the United States, of the so-called "Volcker" rule named after the former chairman of the Federal Reserve that inspired it. This is also the subject of the measures recently put in place in France and Germany - which are inspired by the same philosophy. It is not surprising that our two countries, the first in Europe to initiate legislation in this area, are today reluctant to adopt a Brussels project of very different inspiration. As for the idea of leaving a margin of appreciation to the supervisor to judge the activities that must be confined, this good provision exists in French law. But this does not fundamentally change the essential question: what operations are useful or not to the real economy? And what are the real risky operations? If we start with bad reasoning, there is little chance that we will end up with a good result. And I judged it my duty to say it clearly, and without waiting.
text_original: Tribune de Christian Noyer, Gouverneur de la Banque de France parue dans Le Monde  le 12 fvrier 2014  Prservons le financement des entreprises  La Commission europenne a rcemment prsent des propositions sur la sparation, au sein des banques, des activits de march. J'ai exprim,  ce sujet, de vives rserves. Mes propos ont pu surprendre. Le Gouverneur de la Banque de France prside l'autorit de supervision des banques (lACPR). Comment peut-il s'opposer  une initiative qui vise  rduire les risques, protger le contribuable, et lutter contre une concentration excessive et dangereuse des activits bancaires ? L'objectif poursuivi par la Commission est lgitime, mais les modalits retenues sont dangereuses car elles touchent directement au financement des entreprises. Ses propositions procdent d'une vision fausse, selon laquelle il existe d'un ct les banques qui font du crdit et de l'autre les marchs financiers qui concentrent des risques inutiles  l'conomie. Ce n'est plus le cas aujourd'hui. La crise nous a appris, au contraire, que la finance forme un tout. Les banques et les marchs interagissent constamment dans le financement des entreprises de toutes tailles. C'est vrai en temps de crise ; cest aussi vrai en priode plus normale. Cette complmentarit entre banques et marchs sera,  l'avenir, encore plus ncessaire que dans le pass. Les entreprises auront toujours besoin des banques, soit pour des prts classiques, soit pour lever des fonds auprs d'investisseurs. Mais les nouvelles exigences prudentielles  qui renforcent la solidit des banques  conduiront aussi  une distribution plus slective du crdit. Il est souhaitable que les entreprises, y compris les petites et moyennes, puissent mettre des actions et obligations et trouver des financements sur les marchs comme auprs des banques. Le dveloppement d'une titrisation saine -  travers des instruments transparents, simples, homognes, rglements et surveills - devrait y aider puissamment. Les banques doivent aussi pouvoir faire appel aux grands intermdiaires qui grent l'pargne des Franais. Et les investisseurs, particuliers, petites mutuelles, caisses de retraite complmentaires, gestionnaires de SICAV, devront trouver les banques capables dassurer la liquidit de leurs investissements. Une conomie saine repose donc sur des relations stables, robustes et contrles entre les banques, les entreprises, les compagnies d'assurance, les caisses de retraite et les OPCVM. C'est--dire sur des marchs financiers profonds, liquides, fonctionnels et bien rguls. Vouloir isoler totalement les uns des autres, c'est freiner le financement des entreprises, freiner les investissements, pnaliser l'pargne et rduire la croissance. La sparation des activits, y compris sous forme de filialisation, telle que propose par la Commission europenne conduirait probablement  de trs grosses difficults de financements pour nos entreprises. Par exemple, la tenue de march par les banques nest pas une activit fortement rmunratrice. Si elle disparat, quels investisseurs accepteront dacheter les obligations dentreprises sans perspective de pouvoir les revendre facilement en cas de besoin ? Ltat lui-mme serait gravement touch pour lmission de sa dette. De mme, les ressources leves, sans laide de sa maison-mre, par une filiale spcialise, seront limites et trs chres. Je ne crois pas, dans ces conditions, que les banques pourraient continuer  apporter le mme service, et au mme cot, aux ETI et aux PME. Je ne pense pas qu'elles pourraient assurer le mme accompagnement de nos entreprises  lexportation, en grant dans une mme relation avec les entreprises, leurs besoins de crdits de toute sorte, leurs oprations de change, leurs besoins de refinancement sur les marchs. C'est une illusion, en outre, de penser qu'une spcialisation totale des banques  travers la sparation des activits renforcerait la scurit. Notre exprience est inverse. Au cours de la crise, les plus grands sinistres bancaires se sont produits dans des banques trs spcialises. Lehman Brothers tait une pure banque dinvestissement, de mme que Bear Stearns. Northern Rock, qui a t le plus bel exemple de panique bancaire, tait une pure banque de dtail. Par contraste, les grandes banques universelles, donc diversifies, ont mieux rsist aux chocs. Depuis cinq ans, la communaut internationale, sous lgide du G20, a ralis de grands progrs dans la rglementation des activits financires. Le Commissaire europen Michel Barnier y a pris une part importante  et je veux ici trs sincrement lui en rendre hommage. Le renforcement des fonds propres des banques, particulirement fort pour les grandes banques dites systmiques, limposition d'exigences de liquidit, la mise en place de systmes de rsolution, le dveloppement d'une supervision renforce et plus rigoureuse, constituent des avances majeures. Dans ce nouveau paysage prudentiel, une rglementation des activits de march a toute sa place. Il est lgitime, en particulier, d'interdire  une banque de prendre des positions directionnelles pour son compte propre. Cest l'objet, aux tats-Unis de la rgle dite "Volcker" du nom de lancien prsident de la Rserve fdrale qui la inspire. C'est aussi l'objet des mesures rcemment mises en place en France et en Allemagne  qui s'inspirent de la mme philosophie. Il est peu surprenant que nos deux pays, les premiers en Europe  initier des lgislations dans ce domaine, soient aujourd'hui rticents vis--vis d'un projet bruxellois d'inspiration trs diffrente. Quant  lide de laisser une marge dapprciation au superviseur pour juger des activits qui doivent tre cantonnes, cette bonne disposition existe dans la loi franaise. Mais cela ne change pas fondamentalement la question essentielle : quelles sont les oprations utiles ou pas  lconomie relle ? Et quelles sont vraiment les oprations risques ? Si lon part sur de mauvais raisonnements, il y a peu de chances que lon aboutisse  un bon rsultat. Et jai jug de mon devoir de le dire avec nettet, et sans attendre.

Title: e For financing of companies by insurers
text: Op-ed by Robert Ophe8le, Deputy Governor of the Banque de France, published in L'Opinion - April 8, 2014 "For financing of companies by insurers" The financing of companies by insurers is a necessary development in a context of relative decline in the banking system and the development of market financing. It is still necessary to surround oneself with certain precautions to avoid asymmetries of information and to put in place a good risk management. First, some elements of inventory. In twenty years, households' investments in life insurance have increased from 50% to 125% of their bank deposits and the total assets of the insurance sector have increased 5-fold to more than 2,000 billion euros. However, this resource has not fully benefited the French economy since just over 50% of these assets are invested in France and the share that directly finances French non-financial companies represents only 8% of total assets: 2/3 in shares and only a third in receivables; or less than 50 billion for the latter with most of it in bonds. This amount must be compared to the 1,400 billion in corporate debt, including 800 billion in bank loans. This allocation of savings was indirectly favourable to our economy since it ensured good financing of the banking system - with 21% of total investments, banks are also the main beneficiaries of the funds collected by insurers. However, this model cannot continue as it stands because the new banking regulations weigh on the ability of banks to finance the economic recovery that would require an increase in the supply of credit. The LCR liquidity ratio penalizes them because they have few deposits from particular customers, deemed the most stable by regulation; this is the flip side of the success of life insurance and centralized regulated savings at the Caisse des De9pf4ts et Consignations. The leverage ratio pushes them to reduce the size of their balance sheet. Finally, the increased weighting of derivatives has increased the cost of equity of project and infrastructure financing provided so far by banks. A first solution would be to redirect part of the savings collected by insurers to the banks' balance sheets, but it is more effective to direct part of the insurers' investments directly towards the financing of French companies. This approach has become an important element in the reflection of a policy aimed at promoting non-bank financing. Rights and duties of investors. Such an evolution must be possible provided that a prudent approach, good risk control and a controlled and transparent framework are taken. Banks are in a privileged position to manage credit risk on companies: they keep their accounts and therefore have close information on possible cash flow problems; they offer a wide range of financing solutions and maintain a close relationship with business leaders who are often reluctant to widen the circle of third parties kept informed of their situation and strategy; finally, they have a depth of data that allows them to properly structure the governance of their risks. In addition, bank financing benefits from the mechanism of money creation that makes it possible to distribute credit and refinance it if the market is functioning well and if the central bank plays its role as lender of last resort; this is especially true in France where we are refinancing banks with corporate loans as collateral. But, faced with less recourse to bank credit, the Banque de France intends to promote the controlled development of non-bank financing, especially by insurers. Since August 2013, companies governed by the Insurance Code have been authorized to grant unsecured loans to unlisted companies, but these loans must thus be part of a program specifically approved by the ACPR, the approval taking into account in particular the adequacy of the institution's credit risk analysis and measurement system. With regard to investment vehicles, private placement appears to be particularly interesting. To support the development of the French EuroPP market and especially to attract "small" mid-caps, the CCIP Paris-Ile-de-France and the Banque de France initiated last summer a reflection of Place which resulted in a charter, now adopted by the professional associations, which specifies the rights and duties of investors of companies and arranging banks and ensures equal treatment between bank creditors and investors in EuroPP. The financing of companies can also go through securitization. The landscape is currently too complex and it is also important to standardize: no complex arrangement (no securitization of securitization), exit from the balance sheets of banks only when the direct risk is controllable by the investor. It is in this latter perspective that the Banque de France supports the initiative to create a securitisation vehicle for SME loans, a non-consolidating securitisation but fed by claims on companies with a "good" Banque de France rating. A first issue of 2 to 3 billion euros is expected in the coming days. This refinancing medium will be an asset likely to be of interest to insurers. Corporate credit is first and foremost a banker's job, but there is a clear need for a significant contribution from the insurance sector to this financing; it is an opportunity for companies to have direct access to the final investor as long as this is done in a clear framework with an assumed sharing of risks.
text_original: Tribune de Robert Ophle, Sous-gouverneur de la Banque de France, parue dans LOpinion  le 8 avril 2014  Pour un financement des entreprises par les assureurs  Le financement des entreprises par les assureurs est une volution ncessaire dans un contexte de relatif repli du systme bancaire et de dveloppement des financements de march. Encore faut-il s'entourer de certaines prcautions pour viter les asymtries d'informations et mettre en place une bonne gestion des risques. D'abord quelques lments d'tat des lieux. En vingt ans, les placements des mnages en assurance-vie sont passs de 50%  125% de leurs dpts bancaires et le total des actifs du secteur de l'assurance a t multipli par 5  plus de 2 000 milliards d'euros. Pourtant, cette ressource n'a pas pleinement profit  l'conomie franaise puisqu' peine plus de 50% de ces actifs sont investis en France et la part qui finance directement les socits nonfinancires franaises reprsente seulement 8% du total des actifs : les 2/3 en actions et le tiers seulement en crances ; soit moins de 50 milliards pour ces dernires avec l'essentiel en obligations. Ce montant doit tre mis en regard des 1 400 milliards d'endettement des socits dont 800 milliards en crdits bancaires. Cette allocation de l'pargne tait favorable  notre conomie de faon indirecte puisqu'elle assurait un bon financement du systme bancaire - avec 21% du total des placements, les banques sont d'ailleurs les premires bnficiaires des fonds collects par les assureurs. Pourtant, ce modle ne peut perdurer en l'tat car les nouvelles rglementations bancaires psent sur la capacit des banques  financer la reprise conomique qui ncessiterait une augmentation de l'offre de crdit. Le ratio de liquidit LCR les pnalise car elles ne disposent que de peu de dpts de clientle particulire, rputs les plus stables par la rglementation; c'est le revers du succs de l'assurance vie et de l'pargne rglemente centralise  la Caisse des Dpts et Consignations. Le ratio de levier les pousse  rduire la taille de leur bilan. Enfin, la pondration accrue des drivs a augment le cot en fonds propres des financements de projet et d'infrastructures accords jusqu'ici par les banques. Une premire solution serait de rorienter une partie de l'pargne collecte par les assureurs vers le bilan des banques mais il est plus efficace d'orienter directement une partie des placements des assureurs vers le financement des entreprises franaises. Cette piste est devenue un lment important de rflexion d'une politique visant  favoriser les financements non bancaires. Droits et devoirs des investisseurs. Une telle volution doit pouvoir se faire  condition d'avoir une dmarche prudente, une bonne matrise des risques, un cadre contrl et transparent. Les banques sont en effet dans une position privilgie pour grer le risque de crdit sur les entreprises : elles tiennent leurs comptes et disposent donc d'une information rapproche sur d'ventuels problmes de trsorerie ; elles offrent une large gamme de solutions de financement et entretiennent une relation troite avec les chefs d'entreprise qui rpugnent souvent  largir le cercle des tiers tenus au courant de leur situation et de leur stratgie ; elles disposent enfin d'une profondeur de donnes qui leur permet de bien structurer la gouvernance de leurs risques. Par ailleurs, le financement bancaire bnficie du mcanisme de cration montaire qui permet de distribuer du crdit et de le refinancer si le march fonctionne bien et si la banque centrale joue son rle de prteur en dernier ressort ; ce qui est tout particulirement vrai en France o nous refinanons les banques avec des crdits aux entreprises comme collatral. Mais, face  un moindre recours au crdit bancaire, la Banque de France entend favoriser le dveloppement matris des financements non bancaires, tout particulirement par les assureurs. Depuis aot 2013, les entreprises rgies par le Code des assurances sont ainsi autorises  accorder des prts non garantis aux entreprises non cotes, mais ces prts doivent ainsi entrer dans le cadre d'un programme spcifiquement approuv par l'ACPR, l'approbation tenant notamment compte de l'adquation du systme d'analyse et de mesure des risques de crdit de l'tablissement. S'agissant des supports d'investissement, le placement priv apparat particulirement intressant. Pour accompagner le dveloppement du march franais de l'EuroPP et surtout pour y attirer des petites ETI, la CCIP Paris-Ile-de-France et la Banque de France ont initi l't dernier une rflexion de Place qui a abouti  une charte, dsormais adopte par les associations professionnelles, qui prcise les droits et devoirs des investisseurs des entreprises et des banques arrangeuses et permet d'assurer une galit de traitement entre les cranciers bancaires et les investisseurs en EuroPP. Le financement des entreprises peut galement passer par la titrisation. Le paysage reste actuellement trop complexe et il importe l aussi de standardiser : pas de montage complexe (pas de titrisation de titrisation), sortie du bilan des banques que lorsque le risque direct est matrisable par l'investisseur. C'est dans cette dernire perspective que la Banque de France soutient l'initiative de cration d'un vhicule de titrisation de Place pour les crdits aux PME, titrisation nondconsolidante mais alimente par des crances sur des entreprises bnficiant d'une bonne notation Banque de France. Une premire mission de 2  3 milliards d'euros est attendue dans les tout prochains jours. Ce support de refinancement sera un actif susceptible d'intresser les assureurs. Le crdit aux entreprises est avant tout un mtier de banquier mais il y a un besoin vident d'une contribution significative du secteur des assurances  ce financement ; c'est une opportunit pour les entreprises d'avoir un accs direct  l'investisseur final pourvu que cela soit fait dans un cadre clair avec un partage assum des risques.

Title: Europe 1
text: Interview with Christian Noyer, Governor of the Banque de France "Further reforms are needed to boost growth" Europe 1 - Jean-Pierre Elkabbach - 30 April 2014 Jean-Pierre Elkabbach: Welcome, Mr. Governor, Christian Noyer, good morning. Christian Noyer: Hello Jean-Pierre Elkabbach. J.P. E.: With a majority of 33 votes, can Manuel Valls govern and above all implement his stability program? C. N.: In any case, it is absolutely necessary that he applies it and so I am sure that he will succeed in applying it. There is no choice, it is absolutely essential to recover the economy and to recreate jobs. J.P. E.: Was he right to dramatize in these conditions? C. N.: Yes, he was right to dramatize because the whole of Europe, the whole world, is looking at whether the France will be able to carry out these reforms. Everyone knows that we have a problem of competitiveness, that we have a problem of employment and therefore we must absolutely ensure our credibility by achieving... J.P. E.: If not, what happens? C. N.: Otherwise, what can happen is that interest rates rise, that we have to pay more for the public debt. That it weighs even more on businesses and households and therefore it will force us to make even greater efforts. J.P. E.: The 41 rebels of the Socialist Party reproach Manuel Valls for sacrificing social welfare for the sake of competitiveness. In the name of truth, what are you telling them this morning? 1 C. N.: I don't understand this attitude. The greatest inequality is inequality in employment. And the best way to defend the poorest is to ensure job creation and stronger growth. And that's how we really achieve more justice in society: with a more flourishing economy. So I really think that the choice that is made by the Prime Minister is the only possible choice. J.P. E.: And you're asking them to be more responsible in a way, if I may? C. N.: Yes, yes, of course, of course. I believe that everyone must indeed assume their responsibilities. J.P. E.: Manuel Valls assumes, he assumes the 50 billion in savings. The UMP says it needs 130 billion, one wonders where it would find them. The Attali commission was already advocating 90 billion a few years ago. But then, will the 50 billion, Mr. Governor of the Bank of France, remain 50 billion or will it take more? C. N.: I believe that over time, in the medium term, more will be needed, but for the next few years, this program is already an important program, quite ambitious, and to go further it will be necessary to make reforms of very strong structures in the administration, in the State. They will be necessary, but I believe that what is being done is reasonable and makes it possible to finance both the reduction in the deficit and the Stability Pact, the Responsibility Pact, in a way that is entirely appropriate. J.P. E.: You say that the 50 billion, in the medium term, means that more will be needed? C. N.: This means that, when we look at 5 years, at 10 years, we will have to go further. But I believe that for the next three years it is something that is both realistic and that makes it possible to finance most of what needs to be done. J.P. E.: This government promises that its trajectory will allow it in 2015 to reach the 3% deficit. How many billions more and is it mostly achievable? C. N.: Yes, it is achievable! This obviously requires a very rapid implementation of the programme, so that is why time is of the essence. It will work if we have, on arrival, the creation of jobs that will boost purchasing power, with more people who will have a job, who will have larger and more stable incomes, with investment and with exports. All this is the competitiveness of the economy and therefore that is exactly what the result of the programme should be. J.P. E.: Yes, yes, but these are bets! It is the bet that it will improve and that growth will return, competitiveness etc. C. N.: No, no! When we run economic models, we see what the measures that are taken give, what they give in principle. Of course, we are not 2 completely master of all the parameters, of the whole environment but I find that it is a path that is reasonable, and so the important thing is to implement it very quickly because it always takes a little time to have the full effect. And so we must not waste time. J.P. E.: So Manuel Valls announced yesterday that Frane7ois Hollande and the heads of state of Europe will act once the Strasbourg parliament is in place for a lower euro. Central banker, Governor, you belong to the ECB in Frankfurt, what should it do soon? C. N.: We cannot put the euro at the parity we want; it is an illusion to think that we can decide the level of the euro with a wave of a magic wand. J.P. E.: But has the ECB injected enough liquidity to finance Europe's economy? C. N.: The ECB has injected a lot of liquidity. We finance banks in the euro area on an open window so that they can make all the necessary credit; we have put our interest rates at a very low level, at a level that is equivalent to that of the US Fed... J.P. E.: But what would you personally recommend to the ECB for its future advice? Because it is expected and there is an electoral campaign for the European elections on 25th May. We will hear and we hear: it is the fault of the euro, it is the fault of the euro, let us get rid of the euro. C. N.: No, that's an illusion. We have never had such low interest rates. We now have interest rates that are lower than U.S. rates over virtually every yield period, which is called the entire yield curve. We have refinancing rates for example from Germany and France that are lower than the 10-year rates in the United States. J.P. E.: Does this mean that we have to be content with what we have today? C. N.: I think that, for the most part, you have to be content with what you have. Personally, I am in favour of taking one or two more measures, such as injecting more liquidity. Technically it means suspending cash reversals, it doesn't matter. I think we can do a little more but, for the most part, we have done everything necessary and we have achieved results that are for the moment exactly what could be achieved. J.P. E.: You yourself repeat that Manuel Valls must go even further. Further on, where is it? C. N.: Further, it is in reforms that will boost growth. So there are many things that can be done. There is a very good example he gave with regard to the reduction of the weight of the administration in the public sphere, which greatly handicaps things. It must be seen that public expenditure is overheads. 3 J.P. E.: There are too many civil servants. C. N.: There are too many civil servants, that's clear; we should go to fewer public servants. The reform of local and regional authorities is very important. To give you just one example, last year the wage bill of all administrations increased by 1.7%, despite the freezing of general measures, of what is called the index point. But it increased by 3.2% in local authorities, which is obviously too much. J.P. E.: Manuel Valls is willing to go faster. Is this possible and would we get positive effects? Should we accelerate this territorial reform? C. N.: Yes, yes. I think it should be accelerated as much as possible because it is a way to save money and to save time, to simplify, to have more momentum in the economy. But there are many things we can do. For example, simplifying the Labour Code, which is far too complicated; simplifying the General Tax Code; simplify the Social Security Code. Making things simpler for entrepreneurs. Take an area like housing, there are 3,700 standards that apply, it takes 4 years on average to give the first pick. J.P. E.: So far the housing policy has failed. C. N.: And so far, indeed, housing policy is not very valiant. We have never had so much money in housing policy, we have never had such low interest rates. Yet, so few homes have ever been built. What for? Because there is no building land, because there are too many paralyzing standards, because the procedural delays are too long. So that's what needs to be addressed. J.P. E.: So you are asking Manuel Valls to go even further and implement his plan. A question about Alstom. Alstom is getting engaged, as we now know, with General Electric. This engagement will leave a month for other proposals including by Siemens, probably encouraged by the Hollande-Merkel tandem. What does the Governor of the Bank of France think about how to manage Alstom's fate? C. N.: The Governor of the Bank of France has no responsibility for industrial policy, so I am very cautious about that. What I observe is two things, the first is that General Electric, if it is it, is a company that has many employees in France, that has industrial activities in France, that has maintained them, that has important partnerships, for example with Safran on aircraft engines. And so who is a well-known company and which is very French in a way. The second thing is that it shows that some French companies have difficulty surviving alone, and so here too, we find the problem of competitiveness, of the ability to invest, to develop. J.P. E.: Otherwise we will be absorbed - not to say "eat" - by foreign capital. 4 C. N.: That's it, and so it's one more argument to show that increasing the competitiveness of French companies is essential. J.P. E.: Thank you, have a good day. 5
text_original: Interview de Christian Noyer, Gouverneur de la Banque de France  Il faut aller plus loin dans les rformes pour doper la croissance Europe 1  Jean-Pierre Elkabbach  30 avril 2014 Jean-Pierre Elkabbach : Bienvenue monsieur le Gouverneur, Christian Noyer bonjour. Christian Noyer : Bonjour Jean-Pierre Elkabbach. J.P. E. : Avec une majorit de 33 voix, est-ce que Manuel Valls peut gouverner et surtout appliquer son programme de stabilit ? C. N. : En tout cas, il faut absolument quil lapplique et donc je suis sr quil russira  lappliquer. Il ny a pas de choix, cest absolument indispensable pour redresser lconomie et pour rcrer des emplois. J.P. E. : Est-ce quil a eu raison, lui, de dramatiser dans ces conditions ? C. N. : Oui, il a eu raison de dramatiser parce que toute lEurope, le monde entier, regarde si la France sera capable de mener  bien ces rformes. Tout le monde sait que nous avons un problme de comptitivit, que nous avons un problme demploi et donc il faut absolument assurer notre crdibilit en ralisant J.P. E. : Sinon, quest-ce qui se passe ? C. N. : Sinon, ce qui peut se passer, cest que les taux dintrts remontent, quon doive payer davantage pour la dette publique. Que a pse encore plus sur les entreprises et sur les mnages et donc cela nous obligera  faire des efforts encore plus grands. J.P. E. : Les 41 frondeurs du Parti socialiste reprochent  Manuel Valls de sacrifier le social au profit de la comptitivit. Au nom de la vrit, quest-ce que vous leur dites ce matin ? 1 C. N. : Moi, je ne comprends pas cette attitude. La plus grande ingalit cest lingalit devant lemploi. Et la meilleure faon de dfendre les plus modestes, cest dassurer des crations demplois et une croissance plus forte. Et cest comme cela que vraiment on arrivera  plus de justice dans la socit : avec une conomie plus florissante. Donc je trouve vraiment que le choix qui est fait par le Premier ministre est le seul choix possible. J.P. E. : Et vous leur demandez dtre plus responsables en quelque sorte, si vous me permettez ? C. N. : Oui, oui, bien sr, bien sr. Je crois quil faut effectivement que chacun prenne ses responsabilits. J.P. E. : Manuel Valls assume, il assume les 50 milliards dconomies. LUMP dit il faut 130 milliards, on se demande o il les trouverait. La commission Attali prconisait dj 90 milliards il y a quelques annes. Mais l, est-ce que les 50 milliards, monsieur le Gouverneur de la Banque de France, resteront 50 ou est-ce quil en faudra davantage ? C. N. : Je crois que sur la dure, sur le moyen terme, il en faudra davantage, mais pour les prochaines annes, ce programme est dj un programme important, assez ambitieux, et pour aller plus loin il faudra faire des rformes de structures trs fortes dans ladministration, dans ltat. Elles seront ncessaires mais je crois que ce qui est fait est raisonnable et permet de financer  la fois la baisse du dficit et le pacte de stabilit, le pacte de responsabilit, dune faon qui est tout  fait approprie. J.P. E. : Vous dites que les 50 milliards,  moyen terme, cela veut dire quil faudra davantage ? C. N. : Cela veut dire que, quand on regardera  5 ans,  10 ans, il faudra aller plus loin. Mais je crois que pour les trois prochaines annes cest quelque chose qui est  la fois raliste et qui permet de financer lessentiel de ce qui est  faire. J.P. E. : Ce gouvernement promet que sa trajectoire va lui permettre en 2015 datteindre les 3% de dficit. Cest combien de milliards en plus et est-ce que cest surtout ralisable ? C. N. : Oui cest ralisable ! Cela suppose videmment une mise en uvre trs rapide du programme, donc cest pour cela que le temps compte beaucoup. Cela fonctionnera si on a bien,  larrive, les crations demplois qui permettront de doper le pouvoir dachat, avec davantage de gens qui auront un emploi, qui auront des revenus plus importants et plus stables, avec de linvestissement et avec de lexportation. Tout cela cest la comptitivit de lconomie et donc cest exactement ce que doit tre le rsultat du programme. J.P. E. : Oui, oui mais ce sont des paris a ! Cest le pari que a va samliorer et que la croissance va revenir, la comptitivit etc. C. N. : Non, non ! Quand on fait tourner des modles conomiques, on voit ce que donnent les mesures qui sont prises, ce quelles donnent en principe. Bien sr, on nest pas 2 compltement matre de tous les paramtres, de tout lenvironnement mais je trouve que cest un chemin qui est raisonnable, et donc limportant cest de le mettre en uvre trs vite parce quil faut toujours un peu de temps pour avoir le plein effet. Et donc il ne faut pas perdre de temps. J.P. E. : Alors Manuel Valls a annonc hier que Franois Hollande et les chefs dtat de lEurope agiront une fois le parlement de Strasbourg en place pour un euro moins lev. Banquier central, monsieur le Gouverneur, vous appartenez  la BCE de Francfort, que devrait-elle faire bientt ? C. N. : On ne peut pas mettre leuro  la parit que lon veut ; cest une illusion de penser quon peut dun coup de baguette magique dcider du niveau de leuro. J.P. E. : Mais est-ce que la BCE a inject assez de liquidits pour financer lconomie de lEurope ? C. N. : La BCE a inject normment de liquidits. Nous finanons  guichet ouvert les banques de la zone euro pour quelles puissent faire tout le crdit ncessaire ; nous avons mis nos taux dintrts  un trs bas niveau,  un niveau qui est quivalent  celui de la FED des tats-Unis J.P. E. : Mais quest-ce que vous recommanderiez vous personnellement  la BCE pour ses prochains conseils ? Parce que cest attendu et il y a une campagne lectorale pour les Europennes du 25 mai. On va entendre et on entend : cest la faute  leuro, cest la faute  leuro, dbarrassons nous de leuro. C. N. : Non, a cest une illusion. On na jamais eu des taux dintrts aussi bas. Nous avons aujourdhui des taux dintrts qui sont plus bas que les taux amricains sur pratiquement toutes les dures, ce quon appelle toute la courbe des taux. Nous avons des taux de refinancement par exemple de lAllemagne et de la France qui sont plus bas que les taux  10 ans des tats-Unis. J.P. E. : Est-ce que cela veut dire quil faut se contenter de ce que lon a aujourdhui ? C. N. : Je crois que, pour lessentiel, il faut se contenter de ce que lon a. Personnellement, je suis favorable  ce que lon fasse encore une ou deux mesures comme par exemple dinjecter plus de liquidits. Techniquement a veut dire suspendre des reprises de liquidits, peu importe. Je pense quon peut faire encore un petit peu plus mais, pour lessentiel, nous avons fait tout ce qui tait ncessaire et nous avons obtenu des rsultats qui sont pour linstant exactement ceux que lon pouvait obtenir. J.P. E. : Vous-mme, vous rptez que Manuel Valls doit aller encore plus loin. Plus loin cest o ? C. N. : Plus loin, cest dans des rformes qui permettront de doper la croissance. Alors il y a beaucoup de choses qui peuvent tre faites. Il y a un trs bon exemple quil a donn en ce qui concerne la rduction du poids de ladministration de la sphre publique, qui handicape beaucoup les choses. Il faut voir que la dpense publique, ce sont les frais gnraux. 3 J.P. E. : Il y a trop de fonctionnaires. C. N. : Il y a trop de fonctionnaires, cest clair ; il faudrait aller vers moins de fonctionnaires. La rforme des collectivits territoriales est trs importante. Pour vous donner un seul exemple, lanne dernire, la masse salariale de lensemble des administrations a augment de 1,7%, malgr le gel des mesures gnrales, de ce quon appelle le point dindice. Mais elle augmentait de 3,2% dans les collectivits territoriales, cest manifestement trop. J.P. E. : Manuel Valls est dispos  aller plus vite. Est-ce que cest possible et est-ce quon obtiendrait des effets positifs ? Est-ce quil faut acclrer cette rforme territoriale ? C. N. : Oui, oui. Moi, je pense quil faut lacclrer autant que possible parce que cest une faon  la fois de faire des conomies et de gagner du temps, de simplifier, davoir plus de dynamique dans lconomie. Mais il y a beaucoup de choses quon peut faire. Par exemple, simplifier le Code du travail, qui est beaucoup trop compliqu ; simplifier le Code gnral des impts ; simplifier le Code de la Scurit sociale. Faire en sorte que les choses soient plus simples pour les entrepreneurs. Prenez un domaine comme celui du logement, il y a 3 700 normes qui sappliquent, il faut 4 ans en moyenne pour donner le premier coup de pioche. J.P. E. : Jusqu prsent la politique du logement a chou. C. N. : Et donc, jusqu prsent, effectivement, la politique du logement nest pas trs vaillante. On na jamais eu autant dargent dans la politique du logement, on na jamais eu des taux dintrts aussi bas. Pourtant, on na jamais construit aussi peu de logements. Pourquoi ? Parce quil ny a pas de terrains constructibles, parce quil y a trop de normes paralysantes, parce que les dlais de procdures sont trop longs. Donc, cest  cela quil faut sattaquer. J.P. E. : Donc, vous demandez  Manuel Valls daller encore plus loin et dappliquer son plan. Une question sur Alstom. Alstom se fiance, a on le sait maintenant, avec General Electric. Ces fianailles laisseront un mois pour dautres propositions y compris par Siemens, sans doute encourages par le tandem Hollande  Merkel. Que pense le Gouverneur de la Banque de France sur la manire de grer le sort dAlstom ? C. N. : Le Gouverneur de la Banque de France na pas de responsabilit en matire de politique industrielle, donc je suis trs prudent l-dessus. Ce que jobserve, cest deux choses, la premire cest que General Electric, si cest elle, est une entreprise qui a beaucoup demploys en France, qui a des activits industrielles en France, qui les a maintenues, qui a des partenariats importants, par exemple avec Safran sur les moteurs davion. Et donc qui est une entreprise bien connue et qui est trs franaise dune certaine faon. La seconde chose, cest que a montre bien que certaines entreprises franaises ont du mal  survivre seules, et donc l aussi, on retrouve le problme de comptitivit, de capacit dinvestir, de se dvelopper. J.P. E. : Sinon on va se faire absorber - pour ne pas dire  bouffer  - par les capitaux trangers. 4 C. N. : Voil, et donc cest un argument de plus pour montrer que laugmentation de la comptitivit des entreprises franaises est indispensable. J.P. E. : Merci, bonne journe. 5

Title: Annual report
text: PRESENTATION OF THE ANNUAL REPORT OF THE SUPERVISORY AND RESOLUTION AUTHORITY FOR 2013 Paris, 23 May 2014 Speech by Christian Noyer, Governor of the Banque de France and President of the Autorite9 de contrf4le prudentiel et de re9solution Ladies and Gentlemen, Welcome to the conference area of the Banque de France on the occasion of the presentation of the activity report of the Autorite9 de contrf4le prudentiel et de re9solution for the year 2013. First of all, I would like to pay tribute to Je9rf4me HAAS, President of the Accounting Standards Authority, who recently passed away. He was a very active member of the ACPR college, participating in several of its trainings. He has made a remarkable contribution to us, thanks to his vast experience, his great finesse of analysis and judgment which have been particularly valuable elements in ensuring the quality of the ACPR's action. The ACPR, an independent administrative authority backed by the Banque de France, has undergone and implemented significant developments over the past year. As its name change shows, the ACPR has been given new powers, including a central role in the resolution of banking groups in difficulty. In addition, we all appreciate the importance of the reforms under way at European level, which are helping to change the supervision of the insurance and banking sectors. These developments reinforce the major missions assigned to the ACPR: to preserve the stability of the financial system, to ensure the protection of customers, policyholders and members, and to carry the voice of the France in international negotiations within its scope of 1 competence. But they will also profoundly change the way in which its tasks are carried out, I am thinking of the various aspects of the Banking Union currently being set up. I would therefore like to begin by returning to the many regulatory changes that took place during 2013 and their implementation by the Autorite9. I will then mention the solidity of French banking institutions and insurance institutions which, during 2013, obtained satisfactory financial results and strengthened their solvency. Finally, I will come back to the organization and functioning of the ACPR. Jean-Marie Levaux, Vice-President of the ACPR, will complete my speech on topics more specific to insurers. I. In 2013, the AMF ensured the proper implementation of multiple regulatory changes The many regulatory developments that took place last year can be grouped into three distinct sets. The law of 26 July 2013 on the separation and regulation of banking activities has entrusted new tasks to the ACPR. Within the euro area, the Banking Union has begun to take shape. Finally, the implementation of the new prudential standards, Solvency II, CRR/CRD4 and EMIR mobilized the Authority's teams. The law of 26 July 2013 has singularly strengthened the acpr's missions. It was primarily responsible for ensuring the development and implementation of measures to prevent and resolve banking crises. This development is a natural extension of the tasks entrusted to the Authority when it was created in 2010, since resolution aims to preserve financial stability, ensure the continuity of the activities, services and operations of institutions whose failure would have serious consequences for the economy, protect depositors, avoid or limit as much as possible the use of public financial support. Due to the specificities of this new competence, the ACPR now has a specialized directorate and a college dedicated to resolution which held its first meeting in November 2013. That college will validate the preventive recovery plans drawn up by the institutions and, where appropriate, take the necessary measures for the orderly resolution of crisis situations, such as the establishment of a relay bank or the call for the guarantee and resolution fund. In addition, this law provides that certain market activities will in future have to be confined to dedicated subsidiaries. The ACPR is responsible for putting 2 implement this principle, as the authorising and supervisory authority for these future subsidiaries and their banking group. Finally, the law strengthened the Authority's powers to control governance. She is in charge of verifying the conditions of competence and experience of managers as well as members of the boards of directors and supervisory boards in entities in the banking and insurance sectors. Like the Banking Act of July 2013, the Banking Union is learning from the financial crisis we have been through. By breaking the link between sovereign and banking risk, it has restored investor confidence in the debts of euro area Member States. 2013 saw the negotiation and adoption of the EU Regulation establishing the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) backed by the ECB. On 16 December 2013, Danie8le Nouy, then Secretary General of the ACPR, was appointed Chairman of the SSM Supervisory Board. The creation of the SSM strongly mobilized the ACPR teams in 2013. The ECB has drawn on the expertise of national authorities to establish the future European supervisory framework and draft a "supervisory manual" that will be common to all supervisory authorities in the euro area. Data on the structure of the French banking system and the main risks to which banks deemed significant are exposed were collected. ACPR agents were seconded to Frankfurt at the end of 2013. In 2014, this preparatory work is further intensified in order to allow the SSM to be fully operational by November 2014. During 2013, the ACPR also prepared the implementation of the main texts reforming the financial activities in the insurance sector - with Solvency 2 -, of the bank - with the transposition of the Basel III measures by the European texts CRR and CRD4 - and of the markets - with the EMIR regulation of derivatives and clearing houses -. They contributed to the discussions on the Directive amending the Solvency II text known as "Omnibus II". They have also been involved within EIOPA in the impact study on long branches and the work on guidance texts (often referred to by their English name as guidelines). At the national level, the Autorite9 ensured the preparation of the market by asking bodies to submit documents drawn up in the new prudential framework as early as 2013. 3 In the banking field, the ACPR has prepared the application of the changes introduced by the CRR/CRD4 package, adopted on 26 June 2013. The change in the definition of the concept of credit institution was the subject of a specific follow-up on the occasion of the adoption of the Ordinance of 27 June 2013 on credit institutions and finance companies, a new status for which the current financial companies can opt. The modalities for the application of the macro-prudential measures provided for by the Basel III agreements, in particular in the form of capital buffers, have also been the subject of work, in conjunction with the Bank of France, the European Systemic Risk Board and the Basel Committee. These various texts took place in a more favourable environment for banking institutions and insurance bodies. II. Despite a macroeconomic context that remains difficult, banking institutions and insurance institutions active in France have achieved fairly satisfactory results and strengthened their solvency. After six quarters of recession (between 2012 and early 2013), the euro area began a timid recovery from the second quarter of 2013, which nevertheless masks disparities between member countries. The recovery remains fragile as the consolidation of public accounts continues, but the euro area should gradually return to the path of growth. In this context, the creditworthiness of borrowers could have deteriorated for households due to high unemployment and, for businesses, to weak activity, which would have increased the cost of risk in a context where weak demand for credit from companies weighed on the evolution of net banking income. 4 As for insurance organizations, they could have been penalized by the prolongation of a low interest rate situation that gradually erodes the return on assets and does not stimulate an abundant collection of life insurance. These risks did not materialize and the main banking and insurance groups, active in France published satisfactory consolidated global results that allowed them to maintain or improve their solvency. Thus, the six main banking groups obtained a net income group share (RNPG) of 18 billion euros, more than twice that of 2012 (8.4 billion euros). While maintaining a relative stability of their risk-weighted risks (0.4%), these groups continued to strengthen their "hard" capital, as illustrated by the 4.9% increase in aggregate Core Tier 1 capital between the end of 2012 and the end of 2013. According to the standards of the European directive transposing Basel III (CRD4) and excluding phasing measures, each of these 6 groups has achieved a solvency ratio greater than or equal to 10% ("full CRD4 ratio"). French banks are now participating in the balance sheet assessment exercise, which will be complemented by stress tests coordinated at European level. This exercise, of an unprecedented scale, which mobilizes the ACPR and external firms, will, I am sure, strengthen confidence in the French banking system because given their good performance, french groups are approaching this exercise with serenity. Insurance institutions also had a positive 2013. In particular, life and health insurance benefited from the return to positive net inflows in life insurance. Net inflows thus amounted to more than 8011 billion, including euro and UC support. In addition, the operating profitability of the French groups that have published their accounts is up sharply, driven by the decline in the combined ratios of property and liability insurance; Jean-Marie Levaux will come back to it. The ACPR closely follows the evolution of the situation of the institutions and organizations under its supervision. You will find the evolutions of the year 2013 in issues of Analyses and summaries published at the same time as the activity report. 5 III. To fulfil its missions, the ACPR demonstrated in 2013 vigilance, dynamism, adaptability and repression when necessary The ACPR's approach is reflected in the achievement of control priorities. The objective of an analysis of the risk profile of all taxable persons on a pace at least annually was achieved: the accounts and strategy of 1394 institutions and organizations were studied by the ACPR in 2013. The entire on-the-spot control programme validated by the college has been carried out. These 253 missions were divided into 60% in the banking sector and 40% in the insurance sector. Preparation for the entry into force of the CRR/CRD4 package and Solvency II has been at the heart of the concerns of permanent control and on-the-spot checks. In the banking sector, particular attention was paid to refinancing structures and the evolution of credit risk; the on-site auditors also carefully studied the financing of LBOs, loans to SMEs and housing as well as the legal risks attached to the "toxic" loans of local authorities and the contributions to the setting of market indices. In the insurance sector, permanent monitoring has been invested in improving the quality and compliance with the deadlines for the transmission of regulatory statements and in preparing for Solvency II. In banking, as in insurance, the control of commercial practices is fully integrated with other forms of controls. Thus, 90 on-the-spot checks were carried out in 2013 as part of customer protection. Finally, the control of commercial practices gives rise to a fruitful cooperation with the AMF, institutionalized in a common pole. This same spirit of vigilance and dynamism characterizes the ACPR's action in terms of study work. In conjunction with the control departments, cross-cutting risk monitoring and stress tests will be at the heart of the development of control programs with CRD4 and Solvency 2, which recommend adapting the supervisory process to the risk profile of institutions and the risks they pose to the market, particularly for systemic institutions. The ACPR's action is primarily preventive. But it must also be repressive when necessary. All powers in terms of the level of bank capital, formal notice (often on matters relating to the organisation of risk control procedures) or files submitted to the Sanctions Committee. In 2013, it thus 6 rendered ten decisions in respect of entities in the banking and insurance sectors. In particular, it issued seven reprimands and one warning, accompanied by eight financial penalties. Effective financial supervision also requires a strong international presence. This is necessary to influence regulatory developments and keep pace with the increasing internationalisation of the banking and insurance markets. The ACPR has a strong presence in European and international working groups: in 2013 its representatives participated in 258 working groups or sub-groups and chaired 25 groups, whether in the framework of EIOPA and IAIS for insurance or the EBA, the Basel Committee and the ECB in the banking field. In all this work, the ACPR demonstrates its ability to adapt to the constant changes that affect its field of action, whether they come from regulatory and institutional changes or from the creativity of financial actors. I have not, for example, cited here the work of the ACPR on crowdfunding or on the issue of local and virtual currencies (bitcoins). Thus, in 2010, the ACP had succeeded in a few months in integrating into a single entity banking supervision, insurance supervision, the issuance of authorizations and authorizations and the control of commercial practices. 2014 will clearly be a pivotal year with the effective establishment of the Banking Union. In parallel with the completion, on behalf of the ECB, of the comprehensive assessment of the French banking system to come under direct ECB supervision, an exercise of unprecedented magnitude that combines a very detailed review of asset quality and a simulation of the impact of a stress scenario, the ACPR is actively preparing for the integration of its banking supervision activities into an SSM based on a convergence of supervisory methods. The ACPR will also take into account in its organisation the recent vote by the European Parliament on the Directive on the Re-establishment and Resolution of Banks and especially the Directive on the Single Resolution Mechanism (SRM) which will lead to the establishment of a European Resolution Board, in principle before the end of 2014. In light of what the ACPR has achieved over the past 4 years, I am fully confident in its ability, under the leadership of 7 its new Secretary General, Edouard Fernandez-Bollo, to face these new challenges. The importance of the ongoing transformations in banking supervision should not mask the important work carried out in the context of insurance supervision. I would like to avoid this pitfall, which is why I give the floor on this subject to Mr Levaux, Vice-President of the ACPR, who will elaborate on this point. Then Re9mi Bouchez, Chairman of the Sanctions Committee, will present an assessment of the sanctions activity in 2013 and at the beginning of 2014. Thank you for your attention. 8

Title: Finance's contribution to the recovery
text: "The contribution of finance to the recovery" Foreword by Robert Ophe8le, Deputy Governor of the Banque de France, "Year of financial professions" - 2014 edition Even though the French financial system makes it possible to comprehensively cover the financing needs of our economy, there is a shared diagnosis as to the difficulties already encountered on certain types of key financing and on those that are likely in the event of a rebound in credit demand. Even if it is clear that economic recovery and the achievement of strong and sustainable growth cannot be based exclusively on increased indebtedness, but must above all be nourished by structural reforms and a strengthened self-financing capacity of non-financial enterprises, the contribution of finance will remain decisive and there is an urgent need to adapt the means at its disposal for this. Indeed, the profound changes that are underway in financial regulation particularly affect the France whose institutional framework is atypical to say the least. The France, which has neither large pension funds nor sovereign wealth funds, thus makes extensive use of the mobilization of liquid and short-term household savings to finance long-term investments and this transformation of maturities is in fact not carried out directly by the traditional banking system. Households' financial savings, under the influence of strong tax incentives, are in fact mainly invested in life insurance products, and, within them, in euro contracts without capital risk and available at any time, as well as in regulated sight investments, a preponderant part of the collection of which is centralized by the banks at the Caisse des de9pf4ts et consignations. These two circuits are clearly far from ineffective since centralization makes it possible to neutralize possible savings transfers between banks and allows the Caisse's savings fund to finance social housing in the very long term. As for life insurance, it is largely recycled by insurers to the banking system through the purchase of securities, secured or not, issued by banks. But this model is hardly compatible with the new regulations that are being put in place in Europe for all banks and, beyond that, for systemically important financial institutions on a global scale, a category that includes institutions that provide the bulk of financial services in France, banks and insurance. Banks and insurers considered "systemic" at the global level (GSIBs and GSIIs) represent more than three-quarters of bank loans in France (BNPP, Socie9te9 Ge9ne9rale, Cre9dit Agricole and BPCE) and nearly two-thirds of life insurance (insurance subsidiaries of the aforementioned banking groups, adding CNP as well as AXA and the French subsidiaries of Allianz, Generali and Aviva, the 4 GSIIs active in France). This can be illustrated by two very simple implications of these regulations: 1 ? the centralisation circuit of regulated savings at the Caisse des de9pf4ts et consignations will lead banks to hold equity of up to 3% of centralised funds (leverage ratio) while the risk weighting is zero; all other things being equal, this represents an additional capital requirement of 807.5 billion; ? the appetite of households for life insurance and regulated savings leads to the singular situation in which households are, net of centralization at the Fund, net debtors of the banking system; their savings do not finance directly in the books of the banks the credits to the companies but goes through the detour of the market financing via the subscriptions of the insurers. The penalising treatment of market financing (supposedly not renewed) compared to household deposits (supposedly very stable) in liquidity ratios therefore singularly limits the room for manoeuvre of the banking system. How can we restore agility to our financial system to enable it to finance the recovery? A certain degree of disintermediation appears in this unavoidable perspective; it is still necessary to master the process. We must first be aware that France is already the country in continental Europe in which companies finance themselves the most on the markets, but it is also the country where shadow banking in the strict sense, that is to say by excluding insurers who are supervised by the Prudential Control and Resolution Authority in France) is the least developed. Due to the place of large companies in the French economy (33% of the value added of non-financial companies), which have easy access to the financial market and whose market debt is about double the bank debt, the distribution between market debt and bank debt is 40/60 for French companies, while it is for example of the order of 15/85 in Germany or Italy. For French mid-caps, this distribution is 20/80; it is naturally close to 0/100 for SMEs. At the same time, France is one of the few countries in which credit distribution is a regulated activity that revolves around a banking monopoly that reserves only to credit institutions (and now to finance companies) the right to carry out credit operations on a regular basis (Article L 511-5 of the Monetary and Financial Code). Restoring flexibility could therefore be achieved through several channels: completing the supply of credit by freeing itself from the banking monopoly, facilitating the assignment of receivables to ensure their financing outside the banking system, or stimulating the issuance of securities by companies. The banking monopoly of credit is a French characteristic and the question of its relief comes up regularly in one form or another; it is nourished by various motives: ? a certain animosity towards "the banks", accused of losing interest in the financing of the real economy to focus on market operations; this feeds a "militant" disintermediation; ? the deterioration in the quality of banks' signatures, amplified by reforms that make banks self-sufficient with resolution mechanisms that make unsecured deposits risky; ? the current extremely low interest rates, which pushes investors to seek yield directly without going through bank intermediation. This demand for disintermediation is therefore reflected in a variety of ways, ranging from individuals, with crowdfunding, to institutional with the now extended capacity of insurers to grant loans directly to companies, through the desire to deregulate factoring or the desire of certain intermediaries to bypass banks with private credit placements. There are many reasons for caution. 2 Banks are first of all in a privileged position to manage credit risk, especially on companies: they keep their accounts and therefore have close information on possible cash flow problems; they offer an almost complete range of financing solutions and often have a close relationship with business leaders who are quite naturally reluctant to widen the circle of third parties informed of their situation and strategy; finally, they have a depth of data that allows them to model the cost of risk. More generally, they have structured the governance of their risks. In addition, bank financing benefits from the money creation mechanism that makes it possible to distribute credit and refinance it with the central bank, which plays the role of lender of last resort; this is especially true in France since we are refinancing the banks with loans to companies as collateral. Conversely, non-bank financing presents risks of adverse selection (good loans would be granted by banks and others disintermediated), rigidity (greater technical difficulty in restructuring them) and, due to the absence of a lender of last resort, liquidity and pro-cyclicality. It is therefore important to proceed with extreme caution in terms of easing the banking monopoly on credit. The revival of securitization is now at the center of all attention because it is at the crossroads of concerns: ? those banks who see it, when it is deconsolidating, a way to lighten their balance sheet and therefore to give themselves margins to grant new loans without mobilizing additional capital; ? those central banks who see it as a liquidity injection medium to directly influence the financing of the economy by thus facilitating the transmission to the real economy of monetary policy decisions. However, securitization is not a component of french financial culture, which favors covered bonds which, in addition to a double guarantee (signature of the issuing bank and right to collateral), give the investor a good visibility on the cash flows of his investment with a very satisfactory liquidity of the latter given the size of the strains issued. The issuance of covered bonds is a cost-effective mode of refinancing for banks, but its lack of deconsolidating nature singularly limits its attractiveness with regard to the new regulations. However, securitization presents the same dangers as those mentioned above of a liberalization of the distribution of credits outside the banking perimeter and it also opens up the possibilities of sophistication and opacity that the subprime crisis has cruelly illustrated. Beyond the precautions to be taken to ensure an orderly development of securitization (transparency of underlying claims, no multi-level arrangement, external valuation , etc.) that would justify more favorable prudential treatment, both for banks and for insurance, the development of securitization would have profound consequences: ? It would lead to a very heavy evolution of the banking profession; the bank tends to have a holistic customer approach in its pricing, with some services providing cross-subsidization to others; typically home credit is low priced because it allows to retain a customer. This global approach falls with securitization, the investor in securitization units seeing only the intrinsic profitability of the credits he buys. 3 ? It would lead to a revisit of our guarantee system; the very limited place of the mortgage in housing loans (only 1/3 of outstanding loans) makes their securitization delicate in a European (and global) universe unaccustomed to securitizing guaranteed loans. ? It would lead the investor to renounce, in the absence of the public guarantees that have made the success of the US RMBS, the liquidity of his investment, taking into account the still specific characteristics of securitised credit pools. Stimulating corporate issuance is the third possible channel for disintermediation; it can take either the form of a "public offering of financial securities" or the form of a "private placement". Two recent developments suggest that development can be expected in these areas; the new start made by Euronext, now independent, could facilitate the emergence of a large market place for medium-sized French stocks and the conclusion of a charter of good conduct should secure the growth of "EuroPP" private placements. In all these areas, insurers are called upon to play an essential role because of their now preponderant place in households' financial investments: gradually they are invited to become no longer bank refinancers but direct financiers of the economy. This evolution must be particularly controlled since insurers must cover the commitments made to their customers; it can be all the better because it is a regulated sector supervised by an authority, the ACPR, which has banks and insurers within its scope of control and which is therefore able to limit the temptations of regulatory arbitrage and to verify that similar risk analysis standards are implemented for similar operations. It is in this spirit that insurance regulation evolved in 2013. The Banque de France is clearly in a perspective where the disintermediation movement must be supported but accompanied and supervised in order to avoid an excess of debt that would ultimately be a source of losses for investors and destabilization for the French economy. It can contribute to this in many ways: by disseminating more widely the listing of the 270,000 companies it supports, by carrying out macro-prudential monitoring of the indebtedness of economic agents, by carrying out micro-prudential supervision of banks and insurance, and finally by supporting Place's actions aimed at developing secure arrangements, possible supports for its own interventions. 4
